title: ‘NFL’s Not Gonna Do Anything’ — Former MVP Expects No Consequences for 49ers Owner Jed York Following Arrest in Ohio
description: The arrest of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has sparked a familiar debate about how the NFL handles off-field conduct, particularly when it involves team owners rather than players. But there’s one reason why former MVP Boomer Esiason believes York is unlikely to face any punishment from the league.
fullText:
The arrest of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has sparked a familiar debate about how the NFL handles off-field conduct, particularly when it involves team owners rather than players.

But there's one reason why former MVP Boomer Esiason believes York is unlikely to face any punishment from the league.

York was arrested in East Palestine, Ohio, during an undercover operation conducted by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force.

According to court documents, York responded to an online advertisement and offered $140 in exchange for sexual activity. He was initially charged with engaging in prostitution and possessing criminal tools, but the former charge was amended to misdemeanor disorderly conduct.

York pleaded no contest to both charges. He received credit for one day served in jail, paid a $1,150 fine, forfeited $160, and was ordered to complete an online course.

Despite the legal outcome, Esiason does not expect the NFL to take action. "The NFL's not gonna do anything. It's a misdemeanor. They're not gonna do anything," Esiason remarked.

The NFL has confirmed that it is aware of the situation and will review it under the league's Personal Conduct Policy. The 49ers, meanwhile, said the legal matter had been resolved but declined to provide further comment.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Not everyone expects the league to leave the matter alone.

NFL analyst Mike Florio believes York should face some form of discipline, particularly because he pleaded no contest to the charges.

"The fact that he pleaded no contest to disorderly conduct means he absolutely should be, if there is any fairness, equity at all between players and owners, he'll receive some form of discipline," Florio said.

Florio's comments raise questions about whether the NFL applies its conduct standards consistently across the board.

The league's Personal Conduct Policy states that owners and senior executives are held to a higher standard than players, yet players have historically faced fines and suspensions for off-field incidents, while consequences for owners have been far less common.

For now, the NFL has only said that it will review York's case.

If the league ultimately takes no action, it could add to the criticism that owners face fewer consequences for off-field conduct than the players who represent their franchises on the field.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

fullText:
Toronto Blue Jays manager John Schneider dropped a blunt quote on outfielder Nathan Lukes after the team lost 5-3 to the Kansas City Royals.

The Royals took a 5-1 lead into the bottom of the ninth inning, but with two runners on base, Lukes hit the ball into the outfield, driving in two runs. However, Lukes tried to stretch his hit into a double, and he was thrown out at second base to end the game, a decision that has his manager questioning his decision-making on the basepaths following the Blue Jays' loss.

Speaking to Toronto reporters after the game, Schneider shared the following reaction to Lukes getting thrown out at second base to end the game.

"John Schneider says that Nathan Lukes should have 'put the brakes on and kept the inning going' in that spot. 'Everything gets magnified when youâre not scoring. Then, I think you get a little over anxious when youâre trying to make something happen.' #BlueJays," Schneider said.

The Blue Jays' loss on Tuesday to the Royals dropped their record this season to 64-69, and they are now 2.5 GB of the third and final American League Wild Card spot, which is currently occupied by the Texas Rangers and the Cleveland Guardians, who are each 66-66 with a .500 record.

Toronto simply cannot be making these types of costly, game-losing mistakes, as they need to win every game they can right now if they are going to make the playoffs. Had Lukes just taken his single and stayed at first base — he ran through the stop sign put up by first-base coach Mark Budzinski — then the Blue Jays would have had Vladimir Guerrero Jr. up at the plate representing the game-tying run.

Instead, the Blue Jays lost the game as Lukes unwisely got thrown out at second base trying to stretch a single into a double.

We'll see how the final few weeks of this season play out, but it's possible this latest blunder could prove to be very costly in the standings.

title: Giants news: Jaxson Dart reveals what stands out most about John Harbaugh
description: The New York Giants are ushering in a brand-new era , and young quarterback Jaxson Dart is already buying into the leadership at the top. As the Giants navigate training camp and prepare for the upcoming campaign, Dart opened up about what has impressed him most regarding new head coach John Harbaugh . fullText:
Giants news: Jaxson Dart reveals what stands out most about John Harbaugh appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The New York Giants are ushering in a brand-new era, and young quarterback Jaxson Dart is already buying into the leadership at the top.

As the Giants navigate training camp and prepare for the upcoming campaign, Dart opened up about what has impressed him most regarding new head coach John Harbaugh. While Harbaugh brings a proven championship track record and intense detail to East Rutherford, the young signal-caller pointed to something much more personal as his standout trait.

"The biggest thing that stands out with him is his relationships with his players," Dart said when reflecting on Harbaugh's impact on the locker room.

— SiriusXM NFL Radio (@SiriusXMNFL) August 25, 2026

That player-first dynamic has already paid off during on-field adversity this preseason. In the Giants' 13-10 preseason clash against the Minnesota Vikings, Dart got a firsthand taste of Harbaugh's protective leadership. After taking a brutal unblocked hit from blitzing safety Jay Ward that sent the quarterback to the medical tent to be evaluated, Harbaugh did not mince words postgame.

While Dart cleared evaluation and quickly returned to bounce back in style, completing 3 of 4 passes for 26 yards, capped off by a 15-yard touchdown strike to rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields, Harbaugh immediately focused on protecting his young passer.

"We just keep playing football, and we'll just try to do a better job of protecting him," Harbaugh said firmly. "And there's no way he should have been hit there."

That unwavering backing speaks volumes to a developing quarterback. For a franchise aiming to build a winning culture, Harbaugh's mix of high accountability and genuine connection is already establishing a strong foundation with Dart leading the charge under center.

title: ‘Classless’ – Stephen A. Smith slams Enes Kanter after incident at Fever game
description: Stephen A. Smith might agree with the stance that trans athletes should not play in the WNBA, but even he can’t defend Enes Kanter’s recent actions.
fullText:
Stephen A. Smith might agree with the stance that trans athletes should not play in the WNBA, but even he can't defend Enes Kanter's recent actions.

The debate over trans athletes in the WNBA continues spiralling every day, with former NBA player Enes Kanter specifically using the situation to declare for the WNBA Draft to force changes to the WNBA CBA.

Kanter escalated the situation by attending the Sky vs. Fever game on Sunday as a courtside fan who was later removed from the arena after an incident with Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

Smith took to his personal show to discuss Kanter's behaviour, criticising the 33-year-old for agitating the on-court players when they are just trying to do their jobs.

"What Enes Kanter did, although he had every right to do it… I think Enes Kanter was very wrong. It was a classless thing for him to do, because the ladies who are playing have nothing to do with this, and they don't deserve to be agitated."

Smith is against the WNBA's vague rules on gender eligibility in the current CBA, but doesn't agree with Kanter's way of forcing the issue politically and then bringing that politics as a fan who is courtside.

The Sky have since banned Kanter from attending their games in the future, although a WNBA-wide ban is not in effect for the center, who also hopes to enter the WNBA Draft as long as the current CBA is vaguely-worded.

Sky veteran Natasha Cloud had words for Kanter while he was courtside after making a tough layup, with Kanter's response to that being standing up with his arms wide open, which led to his removal from the game.

Kanter has since claimed that Cloud made remarks about him wanting to sleep with Sophie Cunningham, which has not been confirmed by anybody on the court for that moment.

Kanter was allowed to attend the game until that incident in the third quarter as there were no real grounds to eject him, but getting into it with a player definitely gave the Sky the reasoning they needed to remove him for that game and now, ban him for the future.

title: 1. FSV Mainz 05 2026/27 season preview: Transfers, pre-season, predicted lineup and predictions
description: After a disastrous start under Bo Henriksen saw Mainz languishing in the bottom two heading into December, relegation looked a real possibility for the club despite securing European football just a s...
fullText:
After a disastrous start under Bo Henriksen saw Mainz languishing in the bottom two heading into December, relegation looked a real possibility for the club despite securing European football just a season earlier.

With the club's hierarchy unable to hold out any longer, they pulled the trigger on the Dane before appointing Urs Fischer as their new head coach in December.

After a steady but unspectacular end to 2025 in his first few games in charge, the 05ers never looked back in 2026, losing just two of their opening 12 league games of the calendar year. Mainz eventually secured a comfortable 10th-place finish, putting any relegation fears to bed, while also reaching the quarter-finals of the Conference League.

The club will now look to take the next step under Fischer. With a full pre-season under his belt, those around the club will undoubtedly be looking forward to seeing what the new campaign can bring.

Mainz enjoyed an impressive and unbeaten pre-season campaign, winning seven of their eight fixtures while drawing the other.

They looked potent in attack, scoring 38 goals across those eight games, with forwards Philipp Tietz, Sheraldo Becker and new signing Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer all impressing in front of goal.

Their most notable victories came against Premier League outfit Bournemouth (2-1), Paris FC (4-0), Holstein Kiel (3-0) and Kaiserslautern (4-1).

While the Bundesliga campaign is yet to get underway, Mainz have already begun their competitive season, defeating fifth-tier side Krieschow 9-0 in the DFB-Pokal last weekend. Tietz was once again the star of the show, scoring four goals.

Mainz have enjoyed a smart and fairly shrewd transfer window under Fischer, complementing their existing squad with some exciting new faces while maintaining the core of the team. Most of their departures have been players who were not considered part of the immediate first-team picture.

Last season's loanees Stefan Posch, Sheraldo Becker and Sota Kawasaki all returned on permanent deals from Como, Osasuna and Kyoto Sanga respectively.

Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer and Eric Martel both arrived on free transfers from HSV and 1. FC Köln, bringing Bundesliga experience to Fischer's squad. Fabio Gruber joined from Nürnberg, while goalkeeper Alexander Schwolow returned to Germany following a spell with Hearts in Scotland.

In terms of outgoings, Nikolas Veratschnig, Arnaud Nordin, Daniel Batz, Maxim Leitsch, Tom Krauß, Ben Bobzien and Maxim Dal all departed on permanent deals.

Nelson Weiper, Kasey Bos, Lasse Rieß and Daniel Gleiber left on loan, while Armindo Sieb returned to his parent club.

As showcased in the opening competitive fixture of the season, Fischer looks set to stick with his tried-and-tested 3-5-2 formation, which has served him well elsewhere and with Mainz since his arrival.

The spine of the team is expected to remain largely unchanged, with the club also looking likely to retain key players such as Kaishu Sano and Nadiem Amiri.

3-5-2: Zentner; da Costa, Gruber, Posch; Caci, Lee, Sano, Amiri, Mwene; Becker, Tietz

Eric Martel and Paul Nebel are set to miss the start of the season through injury, while Benedict Hollerbach continues his recovery following the Achilles tendon injury he suffered in January.

With no European football to contend with this time around, Mainz will be able to devote their full attention to domestic matters, which should benefit them over the course of the campaign.

At the very least, another comfortable mid-table finish should be within their reach, given Fischer's experience in the dugout and the fact that the core of the squad that performed so well during the second half of last season remains intact.

The Bundesliga is always capable of producing surprises, however, and there is certainly scope for Mainz to challenge higher up the table.

Fischer previously guided Union Berlin to Champions League football, and if Mainz can make a strong start to the campaign, there is no reason why they cannot dream of sneaking into the top seven.

With newly promoted Paderborn visiting the MEWA Arena on Matchday 1, Mainz have an excellent opportunity to lay down an early marker and begin the season on the front foot.

title: A new study of former NFL players' brains found CTE in nearly 25%. What do experts say concerned current players should do about that?
description: The football ecosystem seems to tacitly acknowledge head injuries will not be eliminated from the sport anytime soon. Instead, the NFL, players union and researchers wonder how to treat the conditions that result from this inherent risk.
fullText:
A new study on the degeneration of NFL players' brains sent "a sobering reminder that football carries real risks," the NFL Players Association said Tuesday.

A study published in the British Medical Journal reported that at least 24.5% of former players' brains studied showed signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative condition diagnosed from X-rays showing abnormal protein clumps. As of now, the condition has been diagnosed only after death. The study analyzed the brains of former players who died between 2016 and 2021.

The union told its players in an email blast that the findings "should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem." The NFL issued a statement that similarly preached proactive healthcare.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing," an NFL spokesperson said in a statement obtained by Yahoo Sports, in part. "We encourage former players to utilize these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

Identifying and seeking treatment during a former player's lifetime, some experts say, is an important step that research on postmortem diagnoses can overlook.

Dr. Rachel Grashow, the senior director of research initiatives for the Football Player Health Study at Harvard University, said the study's linkage between brain injury and CTE helps quantify the pathology, or study of the disease; but the scientific community and public definitions of CTE often don't align, Grashow said. People diagnosed with CTE have shown symptoms, including cognitive impairment, behavioral changes, mood changes and movement troubles, the Mayo Clinic says. But the postmortem diagnoses have complicated the ability to discern correlation from causation.

"As of yet, they haven't been able to tie symptoms," Grashow told Yahoo Sports by phone Tuesday night. "You can't connect symptoms to pathology yet."

What researchers believe they can do, and the NFL and NFLPA are emphasizing, is treat symptoms of repetitive brain injury during players' lives. The league, union and medical experts wonder whether healthcare adjustments during the years between a player's retirement and their death — a period often studied less than CTE research after their death — could reduce the severity of impact.

"Head injury causes a lot of conditions that aren't good for you," Grashow said. "But if you treat those conditions, that's possibly the best thing you can do for your brain, since you can't go in a time machine and undo how much head injury you had."

The NFL has tweaked rules in recent decades in hopes of reducing the frequency and severity of concussions and associated traumatic brain injuries.

Helmet regulations have advanced, including the increasing popularity of the league's Guardian Cap. Concussion protocols have become stricter and more formalized. The most dangerous phase of the game for head injuries — the NFL kickoff, where high-speed collisions unfolded often — has been overhauled.

Still, the football ecosystem seems to tacitly acknowledge head injuries will not be eliminated from the sport anytime soon. Instead, the league, union and researchers wonder how to treat the conditions that result from this inherent risk.

NFLPA executive director JC Tretter and NFLPA medical director Dr. Thom Mayer met with the lead author of the study published Tuesday, a union source told Yahoo Sports. Dr. Daniel Daneshvar of Massachusetts General Brigham and Boston University advised in an email to players: "Many of the symptoms associated with CTE are treatable with the right care."

"While we don't have a cure yet, we have seen improvements in players who receive care from doctors specializing in neurodegenerative disease and who know how to treat athletes," Daneshvar said, per the union email. "No one should walk away thinking there's nothing they can do."

The union will hold a call with medical experts in the coming weeks to answer player questions and create a forum for discussion, according to a copy of the union's email to players obtained by Yahoo Sports.

The league said it will continue to consider in-game safety strategies.

In the analysis of 5,000 living former players through Harvard's study, which receives funding from the NFLPA, Grashow and her colleagues have identified several elevated health risks for players.

Head injuries can cause high blood pressure, sleep apnea, low testosterone and depression, Grashow said. Oftentimes, players are living their post-career lives without treating those conditions, she said.

"It's so frustrating because it's like, we don't know what would happen if we actually treated the things that head injury caused," Grashow said. "We could see a totally different trajectory for these guys, but we haven't been doing that because I think there's such a tight coupling between the symptoms and the pathology and the hopelessness."

The league, players association and researchers overlap in their message to players about seeking healthcare as soon as symptoms arise, if not sooner.

In its Tuesday email entitled "New CTE Research: What Players Should Know," the union linked to more than half a dozen resources, including a checklist that players can bring to doctor's appointments to ensure professionals are heeding the most common conditions that have been found in current and former players.

From blood sugar and cholesterol to cognitive and emotional instability, the checklist aims to reduce players' need to research where they're most at risk.

"Playing football puts players at risk for a number of conditions that, if untreated, will absolutely hurt their brains over time," Grashow said. "The good news is that a lot of what it does impact can be tested for, often treated and managed."

Research of former players' brains often receives the most attention due to the fear and uncertainty surrounding degenerative brain conditions. But research of former players' bodies have shown more mixed results, including some encouraging signs.

A 2018 study of 9,778 former NFL players who played at least one season between 1986 and 2012 found that former players' mortality rates compared favorably to that of the general American male population. Former NFL players died at 46% the rate of U.S. men of the same age, race and calendar year, per the study published by the American College of Sports Medicine.

Former players in the study died at 65% the rate of their equivalent U.S. population from cardiovascular disease, the study found, a gap that widens far more for players with a body mass index that did not catapult them into the category of obesity. (Former players with Class 2 obesity or higher suffered from 2.2 times the cardiovascular disease-related deaths than the equivalent U.S. population.)

None of this erases the realities of research on players' brains, nor is it likely to assuage concerns of players and families. But researchers caution against fear and hype that can further trigger players' emotional unraveling or trust in medical professionals.

"I don't want to give people false hopes that treating these conditions are going to undo all the effects of football," Grashow said. "But if we know that players are living with these conditions and not getting them treated, having cognitive symptoms, likely due in some part to those conditions and then getting scared that they have CTE and leading to suicidality, then I think we've missed an opportunity at least to try to address some of those conditions."

Conversations around suicidal ideation have heightened during the last year after Cowboys defensive end Marshawn Kneeland and Minnesota Vikings receiver Rondale Moore died by suicide last November and February, respectively. Kneeland's family donated his brain to Boston University's CTE Center, which found Stage 1 CTE evidence in the 24-year-old's brain. (CTE is diagnosed by severity from Stage 1 through Stage 4.) Documented concerns about Kneeland's mental health had dated back to at least college, per records obtained by ESPN, and the Concussion and CTE Foundation emphasized that the diagnosis "should not be considered the cause of a suicide and is not known to be a risk factor for suicide."

Still, foundation CEO Dr. Chris Nowinski noted that Kneeland's CTE diagnosis came amid the league's current era of helmet and safety advancements.

"We have no reason to believe the current generation is at a lower risk of CTE than previous generations," Nowinski said in a statement. "Concussion protocols do not prevent CTE, because CTE is caused by repeated head impacts, not just concussions. If we want to reduce CTE risk, we must implement CTE prevention protocols and aggressively reduce the number and strength of head impacts at every level of the game."

Conversations with NFL decision-makers did not indicate the latest CTE research will spur any imminent rule or policy changes on the field. More research and awareness about proactive health measures during players' lives appear to be a stronger focus.

There will be some who wonder how well data from a brain bank, donated by families of players who often had symptoms that prompted concern, represents the non-donating player population. Others will look at this 24.5% finding as more measured than a previous CTE Center study that found CTE in 99% (110 of 111) brains donated to the bank. Daneshvar was also an author on that study, which some believe was skewed.

The authors of the latest study wrote in their finding that they hope this data analysis can "prove targets for future research studies and policy recommendations." The study's findings on the correlation between dementia and Stage 4 CTE at death could be among the topics on which researchers continue to seek clarity. Union warnings will continue to ring clear, too.

"Pay attention to your cognitive, neurological, and overall health," the NFLPA wrote in its email to players. "If you have concerns, seek evaluation and support. Early intervention matters. Resources are available today that can help."

title: JJ McCarthy Predicted to Depart Vikings After Latest Development
description: The Minnesota Vikings are predicted to part ways with quarterback JJ McCarthy, potentially in a matter of days. The post JJ McCarthy Predicted to Depart Vikings After Latest Development appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
One month ago, JJ McCarthy was embroiled in a battle for the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback job. One week from now, he could be unemployed and hunting a new team.

So went a take from Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk after McCarthy and Carson Wentz split QB2 reps at practice on Tuesday, August 25.

"With Max Brosmer also on the roster, McCarthy could be in danger of not being on the roster by Sunday, when the rosters reduce to 53," Florio wrote. "The Vikings undoubtedly would try to trade him, since the balance of his 2026 pay ($1.075 million) and all of his 2027 compensation ($3.775 million) are fully guaranteed. The Vikings may have to pay a significant chunk of the money in order to facilitate a deal."

GettyMinnesota Vikings quarterback JJ McCarthy.

But with a thin trade market for quarterbacks because of relative health at the position around the league, there is a chance Minnesota might not find any takers for McCarthy if the franchise attempts to move him.

The Indianapolis Colts haven't been able to find a suitor for Anthony Richardson, a former No. 4 overall pick, since allowing him to seek a trade partner beginning at the NFL Combine in late February. Meanwhile, 2025 third-round selection Dillon Gabriel is a cut candidate for the Cleveland Browns heading into just his second year.

"Ultimately, the Vikings may have to simply waive McCarthy," Florio continued. "However it plays out, it's not looking good for McCarthy in Minnesota. It will be interesting to see whether and to what extent McCarthy plays in the preseason finale against the [Denver] Broncos."

GettyMinnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell.

Brosmer was an undrafted rookie in 2025 and is heading into his second professional season. He is a candidate for QB3 and the practice squad in Minnesota, as it appears unlikely any other team would pick him up if given an opportunity come the end of the month.

Meanwhile, Wentz has outplayed McCarthy this preseason. He also arguably put together a better five-game stretch as the Vikings' starter in 2025 between Weeks 3-7 while McCarthy was sidelined with a high-ankle sprain than McCarthy did across his 10 starts over the course of the campaign.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell afforded the starting job to Kyler Murray — who the team signed to a league-minimum contract in the offseason after the Arizona Cardinals cut him loose while still owing the QB $36 million — before Murray or McCarthy took a single snap in a preseason game.

O'Connell then said late last week that while McCarthy had gotten all the work with the second-team since the Vikings named Murray the starter, they would keep the QB competition for the backup job open.

"We'll see how these next couple weeks play out, and we're gonna do what's best for our team," O'Connell said.

Wentz outplayed McCarthy over the weekend in the second preseason game of the summer, and the two split QB2 reps on Tuesday, both of which indicate that Wentz is gaining ground on McCarthy for the role of backup quarterback.

title: ESPN analyst takes a dig at ‘desperate’ Enes Kanter while discussing Klay Thompson to Miami Heat
description: While discussing Klay Thompson’s move to the Miami Heat, one ESPN analyst had some choice words for Enes Kanter. Kanter has made himself one of the central figures in the recent controversy surrounding the WNBA, with his recent push to declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft.
fullText:
While discussing Klay Thompson's move to the Miami Heat, one ESPN analyst had some choice words for Enes Kanter.

Kanter has made himself one of the central figures in the recent controversy surrounding the WNBA, with his recent push to declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft.

These public antics from Kanter have not been received well by many in the NBA world, as one ESPN analyst used a recent signing to take shots at the former Boston Celtics star.

During the latest episode of the Hoop Collective podcast, ESPN analysts Brian Windhorst and Tim McMahon discussed Klay Thompson signing with the Miami Heat.

Describing how the Miami Heat needed a shooter like Thompson to alleviate their spacing concerns, he described the team as being just as desperate as Enes Kanter is for attention.

"When he went to Dallas, he felt he was coming in to be the final piece… At this point in his career, he's a shooting specialist.

"He used to be an amazing, Hall of Fame two-way wing… He can't do anything off the dribble anymore. You gotta protect him defensively now. But the Heat are as desperate for shooting as Enes Kanter is for attention."

McMahon is far from the first person to suggest that Kanter's recent public behaviour has been a way for him to insert his name into the public discourse again.

Given how visible Kanter has made himself over the issue, there is reason to believe that the former Boston Celtics star is leveraging the situation to boost his media profile.

Kanter's most recent move was to attend a WNBA game between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky, where he got into a verbal altercation with Sky star Natasha Cloud.

This altercation understandably went viral, which led to Kanter making an appearance on Fox News earlier this week and giving his thoughts on the matter.

Many of Kanter's critics believe he is grifting, as he is using the WNBA discourse around athlete eligibility and making a public mockery of it to bring his name back to prominence.

Over the last few years, Kanter has seen any opportunities to play professional basketball disappear and has shifted his focus to becoming a media presence and personality instead.

Inserting himself into one of the most public and divisive sports discourses in recent history is a surefire way to get people talking about him again, and it has certainly worked.

title: Olympiacos Winger Update: Ruben Vargas Talks Advance and Gelson Martins Exit
description: Olympiacos winger update: Advanced talks with Sevilla for Ruben Vargas, Bologna enters the race, Krasnodar pushing to sign Gelson Martins, and Bryan Gil emerges as an alternative.
fullText:
New details have emerged in the Ruben Vargas case, as Italian reports of Bologna's interest in the Swiss midfielder from Sevilla grow, while Olympiacos' negotiations to sign him are at an advanced stage.

Gianluca Di Marzio revealed Bologna's attempt to enter the race for the 28-year-old, noting that his future could be decided in the coming hours. According to the Italian journalist, talks between Sevilla and Olympiacos have progressed significantly, but the Emilia-Romagna club made a move last night.

Bologna are weighing options on the wing, with the possible departure of Jonathan Rowe, also linked with a move to Atalanta, in mind. Vargas is among the options under consideration.

Meanwhile, "Zona Mercato Live" reported that Bologna are considering several players for the position. Along with Vargas, the list includes Samuel Bangula, Ruben van Bommel and Brian Zaragoza.

From Spain, however, Maximo de la Cruz Ramirez says Olympiacos and Vargas have not yet reached a definitive agreement. He notes that negotiations are continuing with both Sevilla and the player, and all sides are optimistic that the deal can be closed soon.

Elsewhere, developments around Gelson Martins appear likely to have a direct effect on Olympiacos' transfer plans for the attacking flanks, as Krasnodar continues to push to sign the Portuguese winger.

Reports from Russia indicate that Krasnodar has already reached an agreement with the 31-year-old winger on personal contract terms. The annual salary on offer reportedly exceeds 2.5 million euros, clearly more than he currently earns at Olympiacos, and it has made the player receptive to a possible move to Russia.

The main obstacle remains an agreement between the two clubs. Krasnodar has moved to about 4 million euros, but Olympiacos does not appear willing to let Martins go for that figure. The Reds and Whites are seeking a sum closer to 6 million euros, and if the Russians approach that range, talks over his sale could open in earnest.

A possible Martins departure would also change the picture for reinforcing the flanks. Kostas Nikolakopoulos reported that Olympiacos may revisit Girona's Bryan Gil.

The Spanish winger is an option highly regarded by José Luis Mendilibar and could return to the forefront, even as an alternative. Vargas remains Olympiacos' No. 1 target for the position, while another club has also shown strong interest in Servette's Junior Kadile.

So, we will have to wait for more clarity on this. Something similar is happening in midfield, where Olympiacos is said to be negotiating on several fronts, including West Ham's Edson Álvarez and Racing Santander's Gustavo Puerta.

title: ‘Literally a Laughing Stock,’ ‘Botched Almost Every Pick’ — Browns, Texans Fans Jaw at Each Other Over Houston Owner’s Resurfaced Shot at Cleveland
description: A resurfaced comment from Houston Texans owner Cal McNair’s wife, Hannah, has reignited an old rivalry between Texans and Cleveland Browns fans. The remark dates back to the blockbuster Deshaun Watson trade in 2022, a deal that continues to divide opinions on both sides.
fullText:
A resurfaced comment from Houston Texans owner Cal McNair's wife, Hannah, has reignited an old rivalry between Texans and Cleveland Browns fans.

The remark dates back to the blockbuster Deshaun Watson trade in 2022, a deal that continues to divide opinions on both sides.

During an August 2024 appearance on the Ultimate Fan podcast, McNair discussed the Watson trade and jokingly asked, "Have you thanked a Brown lately?" She then added, "I thank 'em for all of our players."

The comment quickly became a reminder of how differently the two franchises viewed the trade.

On March 18, 2022, Houston sent Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick to Cleveland. In return, the Texans received six draft picks, including three first-round selections, along with fourth- and third-round picks.

Houston used that draft capital to help rebuild its roster, with Will Anderson Jr. becoming one of the most notable players acquired through the picks.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

For Browns fans, however, the trade remains a source of frustration. Cleveland gave Watson a fully guaranteed $230 million contract, but injuries and suspension limited him to fewer than 20 starts during his first four seasons with the team.

With McNair's comment resurfacing, fans from both sides quickly reignited the debate.

One Browns fan directed the frustration toward team owner Jimmy Haslam, writing, "Sell the team, Haslam, go." Another called Cleveland, "Literally a laughing stock."

However, Texans fans did not sit back either. One fan pushed back at Houston, writing, "And they haven't done [expletive] with it," referring to the picks the team received.

Another went even further, criticizing the Texans while defending Cleveland: "Still a poverty franchise. Still haven't won [explicit]. Still worse than Watson. [Explicit] the Texans."

The debate also brought renewed criticism of Houston's handling of Watson.

One NFL analyst argued, "Pretty crazy that Mr McNair has gotten off completely free."

Another person shifted the focus back to the draft picks Houston received, claiming, "Lol they botched almost every pick Cleveland traded them."

The disagreement shows that neither fanbase has completely moved on from the trade.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

The Browns are now entering another season with Watson at the center of their quarterback plans.

After competing with Shedeur Sanders in preseason, Watson was named Cleveland's Week 1 starter despite his struggles and the backlash from Browns fans.

That decision could add another layer to the long-running debate over the Watson trade.

For Houston, the deal remains a major part of its rebuilding story. For Cleveland, Watson's performance will continue to determine whether the franchise can finally justify the enormous price it paid.

Years later, one comment from McNair was enough to bring the old argument back to life.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Can Daniels Rewrite Norvell’s Story at Florida State?
description: Can Ashton Daniels rewrite Mike Norvell’s story at Florida State? The Seminoles have plenty to prove, and Daniels could be the key to turning a season of doubt into one nobody saw coming.
fullText:
Florida State is less than 50 hours away from taking the field for thefirst time in 2026, giving the Seminoles their first opportunity to prove thenaysayers wrong and show that this year will be different.

For many around the college football world, having actual football totalk about couldn't come at a better time. Between TROs, injunctions, questionsabout how conferences will handle NFL players returning to college, anduncertainty over how conference rulings will hold up in court, it will be abreath of fresh air to finally focus on the game on the field rather than thechaos surrounding it.

And for Mike Norvell and his Noles, who have faced a consistent wave ofnegativity all offseason, the time has come to write their own story. Resultsaren't determined online or in the papers; they're decided on the field. Whileanalysts have already written a story that ends with change coming toTallahassee, the Noles now have an opportunity to rewrite that ending and provetheir doubters wrong.

"The great thing about it is there can be a lot of narratives out there,but we still get to write the story, and that's been our focus," Norvell said.

Coming off two disappointing seasons and entering the season on one ofthe hottest coaching seats in America, Norvell needs this story to be a fairytale that only Walt Disney himself could have written.

With the over/under win total set between 5.5 and 6.5 wins, depending onthe sportsbook, expectations don't exactly suggest Norvell will have the kindof season needed to write another chapter in Tallahassee.

And many fans wanted Norvell's story to have already ended, let alonehaving this season to continue writing it.

"I think a lot of the fans wanted to move on from Mike Norvell," DannyKanell said. "They're kind of waiting for what feels inevitable that, oh, thisseason's going to be a disaster. They're going to have to move on from MikeNorvell."

If Florida State is going to have a fairytale season and defyexpectations, the Seminoles will need starting quarterback Ashton Daniels tostep up and become the hero of the story.

The former Stanford and Auburn transfer enters the season as the No.13-ranked starting quarterback in the ACC, according to Steven Lassan of AthlonSports.

The good news for Norvell is that Daniels won't have to be Superman. Hecan be Batman instead. He'll need to rely on intelligence, preparation andsmart decision-making rather than trying to make superhuman plays every week,which he had to do at previous stops.

At Stanford, he was surrounded by limited talent. At Auburn, he tookover the starting role late in a season that was already over, with a firedhead coach and players already focused on their next move.

At Florida State, Daniels will need to protect the football, make smartdecisions and be more of a game manager rather than feeling like he has to takeover the game. His 24-22 touchdown-to-turnover ratio doesn't inspireconfidence, but there are reasons to believe he can be that QB they need towin.

The biggest reason for optimism is that Daniels has never had asupporting cast like the one surrounding him at Florida State.

He'll have receivers like Duce Robinson, a potential All-American, alongwith Micahi Danzy and Jayvan Boggs, if Boggs can remain healthy and stay on thefield. He'll also have true freshman Jasen Lopez, who has been competing withBoggs for the starting slot receiver spot.

Daniels will also have a running game he can lean on in  OusmaneKromah and Samuel Singleton Jr. Both can make big plays and grind out the toughyards to extend drives so Daniels doesn't have to.

Norvell put his faith in Daniels early, naming him the startingquarterback out of spring practice. Now, it's time for Daniels to proveNorvell's assessment was right, silence his own naysayers and show he's betterthan many think.

Daniels ' success could ultimately determine whether Norvell's story inTallahassee comes to an end or whether another chapter is written next season.

title: Daniel Lyons Out to Prove He’s The Vocal Leader For Florida State
description: Daniel Lyons enters 2026 with confidence, leadership as he looks to become the anchor of Florida State’s rebuilt defense.
fullText:
With more than 60 new faces on the roster and an entirely different energy surrounding the program, Florida State's defensive turnaround won't hinge on one single player or position group.

For the Seminoles, improvement will require contributions across every position group.

But if there is one returning defender positioned to make a significant leap, it is defensive tackle Daniel Lyons.

Lyons enters the 2026 season with confidence that borders on conviction, yet it is confidence rooted in production and experience rather than empty talk.

"I got a lot to prove still," Lyons said. "A lot to prove to me, people in the building, my coaches, my teammates, and people in my room."

That mindset is noteworthy considering what Lyons already accomplished a season ago. The veteran defensive lineman earned Florida State's Most Improved Defensive Player award after posting career highs with 26 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, two sacks and a forced fumble. Across four seasons, Lyons has appeared in 42 games with 13 starts, steadily developing into one of the Seminoles' most dependable interior defenders.

The next step isn't simply becoming a reliable starter. Lyons wants to establish himself among the ACC's best defensive tackles.

"That I'm that. That I'm really like that. I'm that," Lyons said. "Relentless, everything. I'm just that player, I'm just that guy."

The numbers suggest that belief isn't misplaced.

According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), Lyons finished 2025 with a 69.0 overall defensive grade, highlighted by an impressive 73.0 run-defense grade. More importantly, he ranked fourth in the ACC among returning FBS defensive tackles who played at least half of their team's defensive snaps.

That ranking places him behind only Pittsburgh's Francis Brewu, Nick James and Virginia Tech's Kemari Copeland.

Those grades reinforce what Florida State's coaching staff likely already knew. Lyons consistently won against the run while flashing disruptive ability as a pass rusher.

Just as valuable as his production is the leadership role he has embraced.

With a roster undergoing massive turnover, Lyons understands experienced voices need to make themselves heard. He prefers leading through effort, but he has no hesitation speaking up when standards aren't being met.

"Being a leader, I just lead by example," Lyons said. "I work hard. I try to push everybody. If I see somebody slacking, I'll say something to them. Even if they see me slacking, say something to me."

That accountability has become one of the defining characteristics of Florida State's rebuilt locker room.

One theme echoed throughout preseason camp has been the absence of individual agendas.

Lyons believes the Seminoles' willingness to accept criticism from teammates, regardless of age or status, has strengthened the culture.

"It helps us. There's no 'ME' guys," Lyons said. "If I say something to you, it's not that I'm trying to criticize you or down talk you, I'm trying to make you better because we've got to be one."

For a program looking to climb back into ACC contention, that mentality may prove just as important as sacks or tackles for loss.

Florida State doesn't necessarily need Daniel Lyons to become the next Corey Simon or Ron Simmons overnight.

It needs him to become the player he believes he already is the difference maker the team can lean on through thick and thin.

If his leadership continues to elevate the locker room and his production follows the trajectory established in 2025, the Seminoles will have one of the conference's most impactful defensive tackles anchoring the middle of their defense.

title: Ex-Seminoles RB Roydell Williams Signs with Detroit Lions
description: An undrafted free agent signed by the Indianapolis Colts after he finished his college career at Florida State, running back Roydell Williams has signed with the Detroit Lions in an effort to shore up their running back room after an onslaught of injuries has decimated the Lions RB corps.
fullText:
Former FloridaState Seminoles running back Roydell Williams will continue his professionalfootball journey after signing with the Detroit Lions.

The Lions running backroom has been decimated with injuries, and Williams adds a much-needed body atthe position.

Williams presumablywill back up starter Jahmyr Gibbs, who signed a three-year, $67.5 millionextension with the team, and was added to Detroit's roster after RaheemBlackshear was placed on injured reserve. Williams and Gibbs were teammates atAlabama during the 2022 season.

Aftergoing undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, Williams later signed with the IndianapolisColts as an undrafted free agent. He was waived by the Colts last week, andgained four yards on three carries against the New England Patriots in lastweek's preseason game.

As atransfer from Alabama, Williams played at Florida State during the 2024 and2025 seasons. However, injuries limited Williams to 11 games in the garnet andgold, rushing for 99 yards and two touchdowns during his time in Tallahassee. Williamswas a member of the Crimson Tide's 2020 national championship team.

The 2023season with the Tide was his best season, as he rushed for 560 yards and fivetouchdowns. Against USF that season, Williams rushed for a season-high 129yards and a touchdown in a 17-3 victory.

A top 100 highschool recruit and No. 9 running back nationally by 247 Sports, Williams rushedfor almost 6,000 yards as a prep star at Hueytown High School. Alabama coachNick Saban sent assistant coach Charles Huff to make the recruiting pitch thatwould bring the No. 5 overall prospect in the state to Tuscaloosa.

Thescouting report on Williams showed he was physically gifted for the position,having spent a lot of time in the weight room. The scouting report on Williams showedhe was projected as a power five starter in college and an early to middleround draft pick.

That scoutingreport proved to be inaccurate.

Once atAlabama, Williams shared carries with Jase McClellan in 2023, and was relegatedas a backup on the depth chart behind Gibbs in 2022, Brian Robinson Jr. in2021, and Najee Harris in 2020. That prompted Williams to enter the transferportal in 2024, landing at Florida State.

Williams waspart of a Florida State rushing attack in 2024 that gained only 1,079 yards andscored just eight rushing touchdowns in 12 games. For his part, Williams added53 yards and two touchdowns.

Lastseason, Williams rushed for just 46 yards and no touchdowns, and averaged justa little over three yards per carry for a Seminoles team that was the No. 1 rushingoffense in the ACC.

The NFL finalcut-down deadline has been moved up to Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET. With the Lionsfranchise desperate for depth at the running back position, it remains to beseen if Williams survives the cut-down to the 53-man roster mandated by the NFL,or is one of those let go in the roster reduction.

title: NFL Delivers Punishment for Rams Rookie Outside Linebacker
description: Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams saw their first player fine of the 2026 campaign, thanks to rookie Darryl Peterson. The post NFL Delivers Punishment for Rams Rookie Outside Linebacker appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Linebacker Darryl Peterson III is the first Los Angeles Rams player to receive punishment from the NFL this season.

Peterson and the Rams are preparing for their preseason finale against the Los Angeles Chargers, but the rookie undrafted free agent received notice over the past weekend about an infraction he committed in the opener against the Kansas City Chiefs.

It was a different kind of "welcome to the league" moment for Peterson.

In the aftermath, Peterson was fined $4,935 for his infraction, per the NFL's accountability hub.

Peterson is on a three-year, $3.1 million contract. The fine is a fraction of his $885,000 base salary and what the league could have charged him.

Per the league, horse collar infractions can cost as much as $17,911 for first-time offenses, and as much as $23,882 for a second. The fine levied against Peterson is 25.7% of the listed amount for a first-timer.

GettyChiefs LB Nick Bolton was fined for a horse-collar tackle on 49ers QB Brock Purdy in the Super Bowl.

The NFL makes itself clear to the Rams and every other team on most of its rules, particularly when it comes to regulating on-field player conduct. The penalty against Peterson is no exception to that.

"No player shall grab the inside collar of the back or the side of the shoulder pads or jersey, or grab the jersey at the name plate or above, and pull the runner toward the ground," the NFL's rulebook states. "This does not apply to a runner who is in the pocket area or in the area defined by close-line play. If his knees are buckled by the action, it is a foul, even if the runner is not pulled completely to the ground.

The penalty for a horse-collar tackle is, of course, a "loss of 15 yards and an automatic first down."

Otherwise, this was largely a learning experience for Peterson in Year 1 with the Rams. LA will close out the preseason on Thursday, August 27.

GettyRams DC Chris Shula has gotten a good look at Darryl Peterson III during the preseason.

Peterson has been racking up the snaps for head coach Sean McVay, defensive coordinator Chris Shula, and the Rams during the 2026 preseason slate. He played in Weeks 1 and 2.

Peterson has logged 4 total tackles in 69 snaps, per Pro Football Focus.

He is part of an edge rusher group led by reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and 2025 Pro Bowler Byron Young. The Rams also lost Keir Thomas to an injury and replaced him on the roster with rookie UDFA Devean Deal.

LA still has DesJuan Johnson, Josaiah Stewart, and Tomon Fox, and another rookie UDFA in Wesley Bailey. Bailey stood out in Preseason Week 2 against the New Orleans Saints.

Peterson is very much still fighting for a spot on the Rams' 53-man roster.

fullText:
The New York Mets kicked off their series against the Milwaukee Brewers with a 3-2 win on Tuesday night.

New York has quietly been playing much better baseball as of late, and while it may be too late in the season, the Mets should be carrying some momentum into next season. After being up one run in the ninth inning, the Brewers plated across a run in the 9th to even the score, and then the Mets scored in the bottom of the 10th to secure the walk-off victory.

Over 74 games played, Lindor is batting .235 with 12 home runs, 4 triples, 8 doubles, 32 RBI, and an OPS+ of 106.

title: Jaguars Reveal Awesome New Rivalries Uniforms For 2026
description: From teal-gloss helmets to neighborhood-inspired prints, Jacksonville’s new alternate look honors the "904" area code and the "Bold City" team’s 1995 roots.
fullText:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have finally unveiled their new Nike Rivalries uniforms for the 2026 season.

On Tuesday, Nike and the NFL released the new uniform designs for the teams from the AFC South and NFC North divisions. The Rivalries program was launched last year as a way to honor each team's local communities.

The Jaguars' new unis feature black pants, white jerseys, and white socks with black, teal, and gold accents. The helmet has a teal gloss (awesome) with a gold facemask and a "904" to represent Jacksonville's area code.

The pants are black with a teal stripe and a gold trim. They also have a jaguar print pattern, where the names of local neighborhoods can be found inside the spots.

The white jerseys contain an inscription on the collar that reads "Since "95," a nod to the team's first season in 1995. The jerseys will also feature a cursive "Jaguars."

The Jaguars will wear the new uniforms for their Week 8 home game against the Indianapolis Colts on November 1.

According to Action Sports Jax, the Jaguars will have these new Rivalries uniforms as part of their alternate uniform rotation for the following three seasons.

The new merchandise will be available to the public on Fanatics and the Miller Electric Center Pro Shop beginning on September 1. Items for sale will include jerseys, helmets, shirts, jackets, footwear and hats.

Taryn Hutt, vice president of club marketing for the NFL, discussed the new uniforms and the program's expansion.

"Revealing eight new Rivalries uniforms marks the next chapter in a program that is beloved by fans across the NFL and Nike. By spotlighting the launch of the AFC South and NFC North Clubs and the passionate communities behind them, we continue to capture the spirit and tradition of football's greatest divisional rivalries."

The new Rivalries uniforms look like they will be a hit with the fans, especially the teal helmets.

The numbers pop and these uniforms should look awesome when we get to see them on the field. They are a great representation of Jacksonville as "Bold City." The uniforms give the fans yet another reason to take pride in their hometown.

The NFL and its teams have had a very bad habit of releasing too many alternate uniforms. Some are hideous and would have been much better never seeing the light of day.

Fortunately, these uniforms do not belong in that category. They look great, and Jacksonville should have a great team to wear them. It is a good time to be a Jaguars fan.

It kinda sucks that we will have to wait another two months before seeing these babies on the field, but the wait will be worth it.

Congrats to the Jaguars and Nike for a great unveiling that succeeded in bringing out joy and excitement from the fan base.

title: Klay Thompson Makes Bold Heat Culture Remark Amid Fresh Start
description: The Miami Heat officially introduced Klay Thompson as a member of the franchise on Tuesday.Thompson, the four-time NBA champion, was pretty excited about the opportunity to win another championship. He was asked a variety of questions during his press conference, including his take on the famed “Heat Culture.”“It’s all about winning,” Thompson said. “Some people […] The post Klay Thompson Makes Bold Heat Culture Remark Amid Fresh Start appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Miami Heat officially introduced Klay Thompson as a member of the franchise on Tuesday.

Thompson, the four-time NBA champion, was pretty excited about the opportunity to win another championship. He was asked a variety of questions during his press conference, including his take on the famed "Heat Culture."

"It's all about winning," Thompson said. "Some people think South Florida is 18 holes and Pina Coladas but no, it's the opposite. It's very militaristic out here, and the fitness programs are really demanding."

Thompson added that it was what made him join the Heat, especially the possibility of making a playoff run.

"It's an honor to be here and I know what they've done for so many great players who left the franchise they were with, and I look forward to having the same experience as far as impacting winning," Thompson added.

The 36-year-old sharpshooter joins forces with stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. They will play under the leadership of Pat Riley and the coaching of Erik Spoelstra.

GettyKlay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat speaks to the media during an introductory press conference at Kaseya Center on August 25, 2026 in Miami, Florida.

The Dallas Mavericks were set to pay Klay Thompson $17.5 million next season. They were initially trying to trade Thompson before agreeing to a contract buyout that saw him give up around $9.8 million, as per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.

While the Mavericks were assembling a very good team for coach Dusty May's first season, Thompson wanted to contend for a championship. The Miami Heat quickly swooped in and signed him to a two-year, $11.5 million deal. He has a player option for next season.

Thompson brings his shooting to the Heat, giving them extra spacing on the court. It was badly needed after their acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo, who likes to operate inside and will need to pass the ball to shooters to become even more effective.

Despite the perception of being "washed," according to some critics online, Thompson shot pretty well from 3-point range last season at 38.3%. He did shoot a career-low 39.3% from the field, but he'll likely shoot more threes under coach Erik Spoelstra's offense.

GettyMiami Heat President Pat Riley (L) and head coach Erik Spoelstra (R) pose for a photo with Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat during an introductory press conference at Kaseya Center on July 16, 2026 in Miami, Florida.

The Miami Heat now have 13 players on standard contract, which means they still have two roster spots open. They could either sign two more free agents or add more and have an open spot in the regular season.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein of The Stein Line, the Heat have several options remaining, like Nick Richards, Gabe Vincent and Keshad Johnson. Richards has reportedly been working out in Miami, while Vincent and Johnson are former Heat players.

The Heat are $5.2 million below the second apron, so they have enough money to sign two veterans on minimum deals.

title: Preston North End vs Everton – Match preview and team news
description: David Moyes returns to Deepdale on Wednesday for a Carabao Cup second-round tie with a personal edge, the Everton manager having begun his managerial career at Preston North End before spells in charg...
fullText:
David Moyes returns to Deepdale on Wednesday for a Carabao Cup second-round tie with a personal edge, the Everton manager having begun his managerial career at Preston North End before spells in charge of both clubs shaped the fixture's more recent history.

Moyes lost 2-0 to Everton in the FA Cup while in charge of Preston in January 2000, then won 2-0 as Everton boss when the sides last met competitively in the EFL Cup third round in October 2004. Everton have not been back to Deepdale in a competitive fixture since.

Moyes' side head into the match on the back of a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace that ended a four-year run of losing their opening Premier League fixture of the season, with goals from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry.

Preston, by contrast, have made a difficult start to a 12th consecutive season in the Championship, losing back-to-back league matches to Bolton Wanderers and Wolverhampton Wanderers after needing penalties to see off Huddersfield Town in the first round. Everton have never won the League Cup in its 66-year history and have failed to progress beyond the third round in eight of the last 11 seasons, a record Moyes will be keen to start putting right.

Date: Wednesday, 26 August 2026Kick-off: 20:00 BSTVenue: DeepdaleLast meeting: Everton 2-0 Preston North End, EFL Cup third round, October 2004

Lewis Gibson is suspended following his red card against Huddersfield and is also managing a groin issue, while fellow defender Odel Offiah missed the Wolves defeat with a groin problem of his own. Jusef Erabi, who scored a dramatic debut equaliser against Huddersfield, is a doubt after picking up a knock last weekend. With Milutin Osmajic having completed a permanent move to Genoa, 17-year-old George Gryba could be handed a start up front if Erabi is unavailable.

Tim Iroegbunam faces several weeks out with an adductor strain, and summer signing Christian Norgaard is not yet fully fit and will miss the trip to Deepdale. James Garner made a surprise substitute return against Palace after recovering from a hernia operation but it is unclear whether he will be ready to start. Moyes has a strong pool of options to rotate from, with several players who started on the bench against Palace pushing for inclusion.

Heckingbottom's side are yet to win in 90 minutes this season, needing a penalty shootout to overcome Huddersfield in the cup before back-to-back defeats to Bolton and Wolves in the league. The manager suggested after the Wolves defeat that there was a clear gap in quality between his side and their opponents, underlining the need for late additions before next week's transfer deadline. Preston have reached at least the third round of this competition in seven of their last 11 campaigns, offering some recent cup pedigree.

Moyes' side head into the tie with genuine momentum after ending their run of poor opening weekends with victory over Crystal Palace. The performance was not flawless, with the manager admitting his side "could have easily been a couple of goals down" during a shaky opening spell. Everton have won just one of their last six meetings with Preston, though their record at this specific stage of the competition remains strong historically.

Preston North End predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Nicholls; Valentin, Storey, Lindsay, Vukcevic; Leroy, McCann; Lang, Devine, Burgzorg; Erabi

Everton predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Travers; Patterson, O'Brien, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Armstrong; Dibling, Alcaraz, Johnson; Beto

The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports Main Event, Sky Sports Football and Sky Sports Ultra HDR.

title: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad – Predicted lineup and team news
description: Real Madrid travel to face Real Sociedad in their next La Liga match on Wednesday, meeting at the Santiago Bernabéu.Under José Mourinho, Real Madrid are in good form. They began the La Liga campaign...
fullText:
Real Madrid travel to face Real Sociedad in their next La Liga match on Wednesday, meeting at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Under José Mourinho, Real Madrid are in good form. They began the La Liga campaign with a dramatic 2-1 away win at Espanyol, sealed by a 90th-minute strike from debutant Carlos Espí. That victory extended their strong run to four wins in their last five matches across all competitions, during which they have scored 10 goals. Additionally, Madrid are on a nine-game unbeaten run overall.

Real Madrid arrive at their rearranged Matchday 1 fixture at the Bernabéu hampered by a serious injury list.

Mourinho faces a selection problem with seven players unavailable. Éder Militão and Ferland Mendy are sidelined, as is forward Rodrygo, along with squad players Raúl Asencio and Thiago Pitarch.

Midfielders Aurélien Tchouaméni and striker Endrick were left out of the matchday squad after failing late fitness checks due to ongoing muscle issues.

fullText:
Real Madrid visit Real Sociedad in their next La Liga fixture on Wednesday at their home ground Estadio Bernabeu.

Jose Mourinho's men secured a victory at the 90th minute in their opening league fixture and will look to showcase a stronger performance this time.

Venue: Santiago Bernabeu, Madrid.

Real Madrid face an extensive injury crisis ahead of their rearranged Matchday 1 La Liga fixture at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Manager José Mourinho is navigating a selection headache with seven players entirely unavailable. Éder Militão, Ferland Mendy, and Rodrygo are ruled out alongside depth options Raúl Asencio and Thiago Pitarch.

Furthermore, Aurélien Tchouaméni and Endrick have been omitted from the matchday squad after failing late fitness assessments for lingering muscle discomfort.

On a positive note, midfield anchor Jude Bellingham has been included in the squad and is expected to start despite nursing an ankle knock from the recent 2-1 victory over Espanyol.

In defensive adjustments, new left-back signing Marc Cucurella is tipped to earn his first start, while Federico Valverde and Bernardo Silva are expected to run the midfield pivot.

Real Sociedad visit the capital with a considerably more stable squad as they look to rebound from their narrow 1-0 opening-day defeat to Real Betis.

Manager Pellegrino Matarazzo will have to cope without former Real Madrid full-back Álvaro Odriozola, who remains sidelined due to a long-term knee injury.

Midfield options are also slightly limited as Pablo Marín misses out following his absence in the opening fixture.

Late fitness checks will determine the availability of Jon Gorrotxategi and Gonçalo Guedes, who are both dealing with minor muscle tightness.

Despite no summer incoming transfers, La Real managed to retain talismanic striker Mikel Oyarzabal, who is fully fit and expected to lead the frontline from the first whistle. He will be flanked by the dynamic winger pairing of Takefusa Kubo and Ander Barrenetxea.

Real Madrid carry strong momentum under José Mourinho. They started the La Liga season with a dramatic 2-1 away victory over Espanyol, sealed by a 90th-minute winner from debutant Carlos Espí. This result extended their formidable run to four wins in their last five matches across all competitions, during which they scored 10 goals. Furthermore, Madrid are currently riding an impressive nine-game unbeaten streak overall.

Real Sociedad are struggling for early consistency under Pellegrino Matarazzo. They dropped their opening La Liga match in a narrow 1-0 defeat to Real Betis at Estadio La Cartuja, failing to bounce back after conceding in the 63rd minute. Their broader form remains stuttering, with the team registering just one victory, two draws, and two defeats over their last five outings, leaving them eager for a reset in the capital.

title: Barcelona lower their asking price to €25 million for exit-bound midfielder; suitors still hesitating
description: Barcelona’s plans for the final stages of the summer transfer window appear increasingly clear: Marc Casado will leave, but finding a club willing to meet their valuation is proving to be a difficul...
fullText:
Barcelona's plans for the final stages of the summer transfer window appear increasingly clear: Marc Casado will leave, but finding a club willing to meet their valuation is proving to be a difficult task.

According to MARCA, Barcelona are seeking around €25 million for the midfielder, a figure that has so far complicated negotiations with interested clubs.

There has been no shortage of enquiries surrounding Casado, yet none of the potential suitors have submitted a formal offer that matches the club's expectations.

Casado's departure has seemingly been on the cards since the end of last season.

The midfielder was informed that regular minutes could be difficult to come by during the current campaign, prompting his camp to explore opportunities elsewhere.

Barcelona's asking price, though, remains a significant hurdle. The report suggests that the club could have potentially commanded more than €30 million for Casado a while ago, but his reduced involvement last season has affected his market value.

Barcelona want €25 million for Marc Casado. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

So now, the Blaugrana are holding out for a fee close to €25 million.

Casado's agent Jorge Mendes has spent much of the summer working to secure a move for the Barcelona midfielder.

Several clubs have been linked with the Spaniard during that period, but talks have yet to produce a definitive outcome.

Interest has reportedly come from Saudi Arabia, with two clubs monitoring the situation, including Al Hilal.

A move to the Middle East appears unlikely at present, though, as Casado does not want to continue his career there.

Attention has also turned towards England, where Sunderland and Nottingham Forest have emerged as potential destinations.

Casado is certain to leave Barcelona. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Both clubs have been mentioned among the teams keeping an eye on the 22-year-old, although neither has made a formal bid.

The outlet confirms that Turkey has emerged as another possible destination in recent days.

On that note, two Turkish clubs are said to be assessing the possibility of signing Casado, with Besiktas among the interested teams.

The Istanbul side had already shown interest in the midfielder earlier in June, and the possibility of reviving that pursuit could give Barcelona another avenue to facilitate his departure.

For now, Casado's future remains unresolved. The midfielder appears set to move on from Barcelona, but Mendes still has work to do to find the right destination and, crucially, a club capable of getting close enough to Barcelona's €25 million asking price.

title: Manchester United preparing €50 million offer for Real Madrid midfielder
description: All of Real Madrid’s transfer plans, at this point, depend directly on sales and the club have faced a dead end on that front.After all, it is difficult to push for a player exit at a club of Real M...
fullText:
All of Real Madrid's transfer plans, at this point, depend directly on sales and the club have faced a dead end on that front.

After all, it is difficult to push for a player exit at a club of Real Madrid's stature where a contract with even a bench role is something players opt to push through.

Over the past month, Real Madrid have seen two players to be particularly transferable – Eduardo Camavinga and Raul Asencio – but both players have refused to leave and insist on proving their worth.

At this point, Real Madrid are in dire need of a new midfielder despite all that is being publicly portrayed. Camavinga's sale, on that front, is an essential prerequisite.

Camavinga has been exit-linked for a long time. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

As reported by El Larguero in a recent update, there may be something massive brewing behind the scenes to facilitate the Frenchman's exit. After all, Manchester United are now getting into the thick of things.

The Red Devils are reportedly already preparing an offer to send Real Madrid's way – one that is close to the €50 million mark. They see Camavinga as a player who can elevate their midfield and could well make the offer formally in the coming hours.

What remains to be seen is whether Real Madrid deem that sum to be sufficient and if the player sees a move to Old Trafford as well.

As reported earlier this week, Real Madrid have been anticipating offers from the Premier League for a while now. They know full well of the midfield deficiencies in several top clubs and the inevitable offers that would pour in.

Manchester United are preparing an offer for Camavinga. (Photo by Ion Alcoba Beitia/Getty Images)

As expected, Manchester United's offer for Camavinga is imminent and may even be followed by more proposals. All that remains is for the player to open the door to an exit.

In his first league game as manager, Jose Mourinho made it clear that he sees Bernardo Silva and Federico Valverde as his preferred deep midfielders.

Given that even Aurelien Tchouameni is an option for the same position, it is clear that Camavinga will not have prominence.

In case the player opts to leave, Real Madrid already have their backup target locked in place and will immediately activate the operation.

title: A major signing for Manchester City showed plenty against Bournemouth
description: Unfortunately for Elliot Anderson, his home debut for Manchester City only lasted 63 minutes. The England international was substituted due to cramp in the second half of Manchester City’s 2-1 win o...
fullText:
Unfortunately for Elliot Anderson, his home debut for Manchester City only lasted 63 minutes. The England international was substituted due to cramp in the second half of Manchester City's 2-1 win over Bournemouth. However, it may have been Maresca's plan to take off Anderson around that time of the game anyway before cramp struck. While Anderson was on the pitch, he showed plenty of positive signs and it is easy to see how his strengths as a player will suit this Manchester City side.

Until Elliot Anderson was substituted after 63 minutes, he was nearly the best-performing player on the pitch for Manchester City against Bournemouth. Anderson played alongside Marc Guehi in the double pivot that Enzo Maresca prefers to use in midfield. With Marc Guehi playing in an unfamiliar role, Anderson was more than willing to drop in and offer Guehi an option when the makeshift midfielder had possession. That was pleasing to see and showed that Anderson had a great read on the situation at hand.

In terms of what Anderson offered in possession that really caught the eye. As per Anderson's pass map on SofaScore, the Manchester City midfielder received possession all over the pitch. When City had possession in the final third, he took up the 'Kevin De Bruyne' position on the right. Once Anderson and his teammates are on the same wavelength this should be a viable source for City to create chances and goals.

Where Elliot Anderson's radar was just off was with his long passing. He completed 1/4 but it was easy to see how much Anderson's ability to switch the play and break the lines will be vital to Enzo Maresca's side. Also, Elliot Anderson's set-piece delivery looms as a major weapon. He should have had his first Manchester City assist just after halftime as his pinpoint corner was met by Marc Guehi. Unfortunately, Guehi headed a great chance from two yards out wide of the target. Despite this, Anderson's set-piece delivery should be a weapon that City profit off of.

One of the major strengths of Elliot Anderson's play is his ability to cover the pitch out of possession and win duels. With how Manchester City's win over Bournemouth played out, this wasn't a standout aspect of his performance. But you could still see how his energy and ability to work for his team out of possession will help shape Manchester City's rebuild midfield.

Anderson won four of his nine ground duels and made one interception against Bournemouth. They aren't spectacular numbers on that side of the ball. However, Anderson's ability to get in the face of Bournemouth was good to observe. This side of Anderson's game is a pronounced weapon in his game. Once he adjusts to life in an Enzo Maresca side, and Anderson regains his match sharpness, they should spike. Elliot Anderson's performances for Nottingham Forest illustrate this, although Manchester City play in a completely different manner to Forest.

All told, Elliot Anderson's Premier League debut for Manchester City was full of promise. Perhaps the biggest compliment you can give Anderson's performance was that he looked right at home in a Manchester City shirt. As Anderson gains match sharpness and learns Enzo Maresca's system, he showed more than enough on Sunday to suggest that he will be an integral cog in the City machine.
