title: ‘Send help’: LA GOP leader issues desperate appeal after Dem mayor’s campaign vid shocks viewers
description: LA County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge says Karen Bass's viral 6-to-1 matching funds video reveals how Democrats codified electoral 'shenanigans' into law.
fullText:
EXCLUSIVE: Los Angeles County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge issued an impassioned appeal for Republicans to "send help" to Democratic-controlled California, describing what she sees as rampant corruption in the state and saying most people "can't understand the level of obsession they have with controlling our lives."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Hoge addressed the online reaction to a recent viral video posted by Democratic Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in which the mayor said the city government would match six times every dollar donated to her re-election campaign. While some social media users expressed shock, Hoge said she was not surprised.

"The rest of the country doesn't understand what we're living under here," she told Fox News Digital.

"The number one thing people need to understand about Los Angeles in particular and California in general is that they've codified all of their shenanigans," she explained. "What normal people consider cheating or weirdness in the electoral process? It's all in the rules [here]."

Los Angeles Proposal To Allow Noncitizens To Vote In Local Elections Sparks Online Backlash

In a recent viral social media post, Bass, Los Angeles' 72-year-old progressive mayor, said that "when you donate to our campaign, the city can match your donation 6 to 1," adding, "If you donate $5, the city turns it into $35."

Bass said that "thanks to LA's super match program, every qualified donation from Los Angeles residents is matched six to one by the city." She added that after this year's mayoral primary, in which Republican candidate Spencer Pratt garnered significant support, "we had to start over from scratch."

"So, we need you to rush in your matching donation right now, to help fuel this campaign," she said.

Social media users questioned and criticized Bass' comments.

Conservative activist Billboard Chris commented, "How is it legal to take money from Los Angeles taxpayers to fund your own re-election campaign?" Commentator Matt Van Swol wrote, "Can someone please explain to me like I'm 5 years old how this is not COMPLETELY illegal?????"

Karen Bass Ripped After Suggesting Taxpayer-funded Dental Care For Meth Users

Author Michael Shellenberger simply wrote, "This is grotesque."

"Is this a JOKE?!?" wrote well-known Los Angeles doctor and political commentator Houman David Hemmati. "Why on EARTH are LA City taxpayers, who can't even afford to clean up their streets or have water in their fire hydrants, forced to match contributions to Bass' Mayoral reelection campaign 6:1?!? … HUH?! Insanity!"

Hoge, however, said the matching-funds program Bass describes in her campaign video is legal under city law. Los Angeles voters approved a public campaign-financing system in 1990 that the City Council later expanded into today's six-to-one matching-funds program. Donations are subject to caps and eligibility rules.

"Voters passed something that sounded so good; they always sound so good at the beginning. Public financing matching funds for campaigns on a one-to-one basis. That seems great, right?" she said. "And then it transmogrifies … into what we have today, this many-headed hydra of insanity where taxpayers are on the hook for $6 for every dollar raised by a city of L.A. candidate."

She noted that the rule applies not only to mayoral campaigns but also to City Council campaigns, adding that they "Have many active [Democratic Socialists of America] members currently sitting and running."

Hoge said "the message that Karen Bass is sending is the same message that those of us who live here behind the blue curtain have been getting for decades."

"And that is, 'Forget it, Jake, it's Chinatown. Don't try to go against City Hall,'" she said.

Shocking Percentage Of Democrats Identify As 'Democratic Socialists' According To New Poll: 'Toxic Policies'

"We saw Spencer Pratt mount a very strong argument for sanity and good governance. It wasn't partisan, what he was saying. It was pure common sense, and they rose up because they were threatened."

Fox News Digital reached out to Bass' campaign and office for comment.

Despite California's political landscape, Hoge urged Republicans not to write off America's most populous state as a lost cause.

"California is totally worth fighting for because it is an absolute gem," she said, adding, "We are living with people who gleefully would reach into the shower and change the temperature while you're having a bath."

Addressing Republicans directly, she said, "We belong to the leave me alone party."

"California, being in the west, is the ultimate place where you should be free to write your own story. And that, I think, is the number one thing people have to remember," she said. "They need to send help."

Original article source: 'Send help': LA GOP leader issues desperate appeal after Dem mayor's campaign vid shocks viewers

title: Denmark's left-wing PM warns: 'Big enemy has started to grow from within' as Europe faces migrant reckoning
description: Mette Frederiksen's stance on Denmark immigration and border control puts her at odds with Spain's PM, as she names failed integration and Islamist extremism as key threats.
fullText:
Denmark's left-wing prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has sent shock waves throughout the European left after recent comments about the Scandinavian nation's — and the continent's — failure to deal with radical Islam among migrant communities.

Her comments come after the mass migration chaos in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, when Frederiksen criticized the actions of Spain's leftist leader, Pedro Sánchez, during a special session on Ceuta in the Danish Parliament.

Responding to a question from a far-left legislator on Denmark's apparent lack of "solidarity" with Spain against "anti-democratic forces" pressuring Europe, Frederiksen said, "If we talk about undemocratic forces, then Russia is our biggest enemy. The problem is that a big enemy has started to grow from within, and it is foreigners who have come to Europe," according to an English translation.

Migrant Crisis Pushes Italy To Restore Border Checks With Spain, Testing Europe's Open-border System

While not singling out Denmark's integrated immigrant population, she continued, "It is Hamas supporters. It is people who commit terror against European societies. It is people who do not recognize our fundamental European values. It is people who sympathize with some of the darkest forces in this world. So, Europe is threatened. The problem is that we are threatened both from outside and now from within, but it is not because of a disagreement between the Danish and Spanish governments, but because of people with an Islamic background who do not want the open, free European society, unfortunately."

Sweden-based foreign policy expert and author Daniel Schatz told Fox News Digital, "What is striking is not that a conservative politician is talking about illegal immigration, failed integration and Islamist extremism, it is that one of Europe's leading center-left prime ministers is saying it in such blunt terms. That tells you how far the European immigration debate has shifted."

Portugal Enacts 'Burqa Law' Largely Prohibiting Face Coverings In Public

Frederiksen came to power in Denmark's 2019 elections on what Reuters called a "platform of radical reforms to reach climate targets, lowering the pension age for manual workers - and stricter migration policies." Denmark already had some of the strongest asylum laws in Europe before 2019, including a 2018 law targeting "parallel societies." That law allowed the government to "demolish or sell off social housing areas where more than half of residents are from a 'non-Western' background," if certain criteria were met, and refugees in those areas are not eligible for family reunion.

In 2021, Frederiksen introduced a new deportation law allowing for refugees to be returned to their country of origin, if Denmark deemed it safe, even if Denmark had no diplomatic relations with that country, and even as the European Commission deemed Danish legislation on transferring asylum seekers to third countries while their claims were processed "incompatible with EU law."

Since June, Frederiksen has been a leading voice in opposition to the immigration policies of Spain's Pedro Sánchez, telling Parliament, "It is no secret that I and the Spanish Prime Minister deeply disagree on immigration policy… I and we will not accept that Danish society has to pay the price for decisions in Spain that we fundamentally disagree with."

On Aug. 1, Frederiksen joined conservative Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and 20 other EU government leaders in a letter saying the EU "cannot allow mass crossings, the instrumentalization of migration or other hybrid threats to create the perception that illegal entry into the European Union is possible."

Italy-spain Border Feud Exposes Europe's Deepening Immigration Divide

The two, currently the only female heads of government in the EU, followed that letter with an Aug. 10 joint statement saying they "are both proud of Europe's Christian cultural heritage and we want to protect it. We expect that those who arrive in our countries and choose to make Europe their home respect our values and do not try to impose ways of life that we do not share. We believe that this is the right path to protect Europe and our common values. And we believe that millions of Europeans share this conviction."

Emma Schubart of the Henry Jackson Society told Fox News Digital, "Frederiksen is right to name the 'enemy within'. Europe has spent years pretending that uncontrolled migration and failed integration come without consequences. They do not… Parallel societies have taken root, Islamist extremism has been allowed to fester and support for groups such as Hamas is no longer confined to the margins. Denmark understands the cost."

Daniel Schatz said Frederiksen "is essentially arguing that Europe faces threats from two directions: Russia from outside and anti-democratic extremism from within. For a center-left European leader, that is remarkably strong language." He noted Frederiksen's "political formula has been straightforward: protect Denmark's generous system of public benefits and social services, control the border and deny the populist right a monopoly on immigration. For an American audience, that is probably the most important thing to understand about the Danish model."

Frederiksen's position is important, he said, because she did not move politically "because Danish voters suddenly became concerned about immigration. She moved because she realized years ago that many of them already were." He added, "The important distinction is that this is not an argument that immigrants are inherently criminal. It is an argument that a democratic society must be willing to confront failed integration when it occurs."

Schubart added, "Other leaders now need to show the same courage, secure their borders, deport those with no right to remain and make clear that integration into our laws and values is not optional."

Original article

title: How did all nine new managers fare in Premier League openers?
description: Who impressed and who has work to do? BBC Sport chief football writer Phil McNulty looks at how the nine new managerial appointments fared on the opening week of the Premier League season.
fullText:
Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the season with new managers.

The post-Pep Guardiola era has begun at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca, while Andoni Iraola got his first taste of action as Liverpool manager after succeeding sacked Arne Slot. Xabi Alonso is the latest with his foot in the revolving door of managers at Chelsea.

So how did the new faces fare after an eventful first weekend of the new campaign?

The German successor to Iraola came within six minutes of starting his Premier League career with a statement win at Manchester City, only to concede two late goals to suffer a heartbreaking loss.

He will be frustrated at the manner of City's goals, with Marc Guehi unmarked at a corner for the equaliser then a slow reaction for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage time winner, but Rose was also shown in those first 84 minutes that he has plenty of materials to work with in a Cherries side that finished sixth last season.

Rose will have seen enough to deliver early signs of encouragement amid the disappointment of such a painful late loss.

Not a bad start to take the lead after 31 seconds and a satisfactory start to Alonso's reign, but there was obvious good and obvious bad in what he watched at Craven Cottage.

The attacking triumvirate of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and newcomer Morgan Rogers hit the ground running, all scoring and combining to devastating effect.

Equally devastating to Chelsea's Premier League chances and the Alonso revival could be the failure to find a better goalkeeper than the unreliable Robert Sanchez, who was at fault for both Fulham goals.

Alonso must find an answer quickly otherwise what Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers give with one hand Sanchez could take away with both hands.

Tactically Alonso used a back three with Reece James operating in midfield but also dropping back into defence.

Disappointing start for the highly-regarded Sage, who did such an outstanding job at Lens, with defeat at Everton but he also knows the outcome could have been a much more satisfactory one.

Palace's second half display will have disappointed him, but they had chances in the opening period to set up their first win at Everton since 2014. They hit the woodwork twice, while Jean-Phillipe Mateta was wasteful. Sage and his team paid a heavy price.

Sage's unhappy opening weekend will not have been helped by a contract row surrounding striker Mateta that puts his future in question, while he will want more numbers and quality to add to his squad.

Next up Manchester City at Selhurst Park, where Sage will sample the superb night game atmosphere as he searches for his first league win. No easy task.

Tough opener and conceding within the first minute did not help Arbeloa's cause as he builds after taking over from Marco Silva.

It is already clear he needs to make sure Fulham can find some goals, although he will be delighted young debutant Gonzalo Garcia got off the mark. It was more of a struggle for another new arrival from Real Madrid, Cesar Palacios.

The jewel in Arbeloa's crown will be 19-year-old Josh King, who he described as "unbelievable". It is already clear the youngster will bear a heavy weight of responsibility under Fulham's new management.

Ipswich Town have backed Kieran McKenna's successor with big money in the transfer market, £150m on a dozen signings, and Gary O'Neil was rewarded with a vital victory against Sunderland.

O'Neil may just be the beneficiary from lessons learned during Ipswich's last spell in the Premier League, when they took 11 games to get a win and went down with a whimper with just 22 points.

He will have been delighted with the impact of Julio Enciso, who he worked with at Strasbourg, and his early partnership with Brazilian striker Emersonn, the pair combining superbly for the latter's opening goal.

Plenty still to work on but O'Neil looked in the mood to enjoy his cup of tea and bar of chocolate while watching Match Of The Day on Saturday night.

Iraola was spared the ignominy of defeat in his first Premier League game since succeeding Arne Slot by Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th minute penalty – but this was a sobering fact-finding mission for the new man in charge at Anfield.

He did not seem unduly concerned, but both Newcastle United's goals will have been hauntingly familiar to those who watched Liverpool's title defence collapse under Slot last season.

Newcastle cashed in on Liverpool's wide open midfield, a flaw from the last campaign that saw them so vulnerable to fast counter-attacks. Anthony Elanga sliced through Liverpool for the first then six of Iraola's team stood idly by as Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock combined for the second.

Iraola has suggested Liverpool will not strengthen in midfield with a 'number 6' type defensively-minded player. This early evidence (not to mention what was seen last season) suggests he should.

If not, the draw at Newcastle was a red flag showing Iraola needs to find an internal solution which is not currently obvious.

It's all very well targeting wide players such as Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh, but what about when teams are running straight through the heart of Liverpool's team?

Iraola must also find a way to make the subdued Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz look like the players Liverpool paid £241m for. Both were poor again at St. James' Park.

It looked like it was going to be a losing start for Guardiola's successor before Manchester City pulled it around with two late goals to beat Bournemouth.

How Maresca needed it after City were pounded by Arsenal in the Community Shield. The Italian's emotions at the final whistle looked as much relief as celebration. He needs wins just to settle post-Guardiola nerves and ease the transition.

Maresca described the day as "perfect". It very nearly wasn't.

Erling Haaland's crop is not the only new look at City this season, but on occasions there were passages of play with lots of possession but little punch, a familiar pattern from Maresca's time at Leicester City and Chelsea. The use of Marc Guehi in midfield was a tactical twist.

Maresca will have wanted the win, no matter how it came, and City achieved it, even though it did carry a lot of the hallmarks of a work in progress.

Seconds away from what would have been a very significant win against Liverpool, but still plenty for Jaissle to take away even with the concession of that late, late penalty.

The Toon Army were right behind the new manager and his team, reshaping after the loss of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, and they responded with real intensity.

The effort was there, the attacking style Jaissle wants was there, only the win was missing but enough to please him after fall-out from this summer's Tyneside turbulence.

Poor start for the Austrian who brought FA Cup and Europa League success to Crystal Palace, losing 1-0 to a late Leeds United goal at The City Ground.

Glasner claimed he cannot simply lay hands on players and they perform like "Real Madrid in the 70s", but this still was an unsatisfactory opening as he tries to bring stability and success to Nottingham Forest and their demanding owner Evangelos Marinkis after four managers were in charge last season.

He had no new signings in his starting line-up, with eight from Nuno Espirito Santo's team in the opening-day win over Brentford last season, although it looks like striker Liam Delap might arrive from Chelsea.

Every Forest manager needs wins (and very quickly) so to make a losing introduction was a real blow for Glasner.

title: Brain disease in dead NFL players 'higher than previously shown'
description: A new study says at least one in four ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had a degenerative brain disease but the true figure could be much higher.
fullText:
As many as 97.7% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 could have had brain disease related to repeated blows to the head, a new study says.

Researchers looked at 878 former players who died during that period, with 235 having donated their brains to research.

Of those, 215 were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease which can only be diagnosed after death.

The study, published in the British Medical Journal, external, also found dementia was common among brain donors.

"We and others have shown that in NFL players, specifically, there is about a four times higher rate of death from neurodegenerative disease than the general population," said the report's lead author Daniel Daneshvar, an associate professor at Harvard Medical School.

"These findings indicate that NFL players have a higher prevalence of CTE at death than has been previously shown in multiple community based studies."

Researchers calculated a "conservative minimum" of CTE prevalence among those who died in the six-year period to be 24.5% - rising to a "maximum" 97.7%.

They have urged the NFL to take prevention measures to reduce repetitive head impacts across all levels of the sport.

Dallas Cowboys player who died by suicide diagnosed with brain disease

NFL admits football-brain disease link

New research finds link between head impacts & CTE

"The bulk of the head impacts that these former NFL players experienced didn't occur at the NFL level," Danshvar said.

"They occurred at the collegiate level and at the high school level and in many cases the youth level. And all of those cumulative hits to the head added up to result in an increased risk."

An NFL spokesperson said: "The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust - and expanding - set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well being.

"We encourage former players to utilise these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

CTE among American football players has been a growing issue in recent years. A 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement for the NFL limited the number of contact practices.

Following a long-running class action, in 2016 the NFL agreed a $1bn (£700m) settlement with more than 5,000 former players.

title: Irish FA withdraws support for Infantino
description: The Irish Football Association says it is "time for change" at Fifa and they will not be voting for president Gianni Infantino's re-election next year.
fullText:
The Irish Football Association says it is "time for change" at Fifa and they will not be voting for president Gianni Infantino's re-election next year.

Infantino has been under increasing scrutiny since his aborted attempt to sell off a 21% stake in Fifa's commercial operations to a private investment company.

The plans were scrapped after widespread criticism, with Uefa threatening a boycott of all Fifa competitions.

The IFA, the governing body for football in Northern Ireland, had previously backed Uefa's stance without formally withdrawing their support, but have now said Infantino's plan raised "fundamental questions" of the president.

It said in a statement: "The proposal to sell part of Fifa's assets to a private equity firm without consultation, represents more than a failure of communication. In our view, it raises fundamental questions about strategy, governance and stewardship of our assets.

"We believe the time has come for change."

The Football Associations of England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland have previously publicly withdrawn support for Infantino, who is scheduled to stand for a fourth term as president in March.

Should the 56-year-old Swiss be successful, by the end of the term in 2031, his tenure will have been extended to 15 years.

title: 'Change is necessary' - players unite against Fifa
description: A number of current and former footballers unite against Fifa president Gianni Infantino, stating that "change is necessary" at the global governing body.
fullText:
A number of current and former footballers have united against under-pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino, stating "change is necessary" at the head of the global governing body.

Former Manchester United and France defender Mikael Silvestre, who sits on Fifa's Players' Voice Panel, issued a statement on X, external on Monday in a post he titled "Enough is Enough!".

The statement has been shared on social media by the likes of England defender Lucy Bronze, France's 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit, and former England goalkeeper David James.

It follows Infantino's controversial plan to sell stakes in competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors, with the statement saying players "share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world".

Criticising how the governing body operates, it added: "We have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa's current leadership.

"For too long we've seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport."

Uefa chief Ceferin rules out Fifa presidency bid

Infantino asked to stay away from youth tournament

The statement continued: "Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership's ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football.

"Recent events have made silence impossible."

It also called for unity from "grassroots to the top of the game" in support of "structural change" at Fifa, with players and fans getting a "real, direct say" in how the sport is run.

Infantino has faced sustained pressure to his leadership in recent weeks, with backlash from several confederations in response to the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) controversy.

Uefa has threatened to boycott all Fifa competitions, with the European confederation's president Aleksander Ceferin saying he expects Infantino to resign or face a challenge in an election next March. Numerous national governing bodies, including the football associations of England, Wales and Scotland, have withdrawn support.

Silvestre's involvement represents a challenge from within Fifa itself, with the 16-strong Players' Voice Panel having been formed by the governing body to monitor and advise on tackling racism in football.

Infantino has, however, found support from former Barcelona striker Samuel Eto'o, president of the Cameroonian Football Association, who doesn't believe the Fifa leader has "done anything wrong".

"I remain convinced that for us as Africans, this project was something that could have been incredible," Eto'o told CNN, external on Monday.

"It would have reset the balance of power in football to ensure that our talent doesn't disappear and end up playing for other nations.

"Infantino has changed football. He's given opportunities to nations that didn't have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions. He has helped our continent. He's helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that."

title: Europe's Solheim defeat in 2024 'extra incentive' for Maguire
description: Ireland's Leona Maguire says the opportunity for Europe to reclaim the Solheim Cup from the United States offers added incentive before the contest in the Netherlands in September.
fullText:
Ireland's Leona Maguire says the opportunity to regain the Solheim Cup offers an "extra incentive" for Team Europe as they prepare to face the United States at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands next month.

Maguire was part of the team which contested the 2024 edition as the US ran out 15.5-12.5 winners in Virginia.

The 31-year-old also participated in Europe's victory on Ohio in 2021 and the drawn encounter in Andalusia, which saw the Europeans retain the trophy.

Captain Anna Nordqvist chose Maguire as one of two wildcard picks for this year's event in Cromvoirt from 11-13 September.

Maguire will compete in the Women's Irish Open at the K Club in County Kildare this week, her last competitive action before the team contest in the Netherlands.

"Hopefully have a great week here [at the Irish Open] and then a week off to recharge and go again for the Solheim," Maguire told BBC Sport.

"Solheim's a special event every two years and a home Solheim is even more special.

"We've got a young team this year, an exciting team and looking forward to getting over to the Netherlands for that."

The 31-year-old became the first Irish player to represent Europe in the competition when she was selected for the 2021 version and broke the all-time rookie points record for either the Solheim Cup or Ryder Cup with a contribution of 4.5 points as the away team triumphed 15-13.

The County Cavan woman's overall individual record in the competition after also taking part in the two subsequent editions reads eight wins, one half and three defeats.

"It's one of my favourite events. It's a team event which we don't get to do very often and matchplay which I love," she explained.

"I think once you're part of one Solheim, the same as the Ryder Cup, you don't want to miss any more.

"It's competitive, there's no money on the line, it's all just for pride and all the rest. You're doing whatever you can to help your teammates and the team.

"We obviously lost the last one so there's an extra incentive to try and bring it back this time."

Maguire, a two-time winner on the LPGA Tour and a one-time victor on the Ladies European Tour, hopes the backing of home supporters can help Europe reclaim the trophy at the 20th running of the event.

"Home support always helps as well. There was massive Irish support in Spain two times ago so hopefully a few Irish will maybe make the trip to Holland."

title: Judge in Don Lemon indictment asks to see grand jury records, adding to growing scrutiny of Justice Department cases
description: A federal judge in Minnesota will probe this week whether grounds exist to toss the Justice Department’s case against journalist Don Lemon. It’s the latest example of judges’ growing skepticism of whe...
fullText:
A federal judge in Minnesota will probe this week whether grounds exist to toss the Justice Department's case against journalist Don Lemon. It's the latest example of judges' growing skepticism of whether the department is behaving ethically behind closed doors in grand jury proceedings.

Judges across the country have signaled they are willing to give far less deference to federal prosecutors than in previous administrations and have raised concerns about DOJ's apparent abandonment of regular practices.

Federal judges in Wyoming, Illinois and Virginia have either thrown out charges or seriously admonished federal prosecutors for missteps in front of the grand jury. The botched grand jury presentments have prompted a historical review of cases in Chicago and, in some courts, new rules requiring defendants to be notified when a grand jury declines to indict.

On August 18, Minnesota federal Judge Laura Provinzino issued a short but extraordinary order demanding the Justice Department provide her a wide swath of grand jury materials related to Lemon and his co-defendants, including presentations made by prosecutors and case agents, and the totality of communications prosecutors had with grand jurors resulting in their indictments.

Provinzino set a Tuesday deadline to provide her with the presentation by federal prosecutors and case agents related to grand juries empaneled in January and February. Further, Provinzino told DOJ to provide any introduction, legal instructions, witness testimony, closing arguments, and answers to questions from grand jurors.

Lemon's team has aggressively pursued obtaining grand jury materials and had asked for either grand jury records to be provided to the defense or, at a minimum, reviewed by the judge privately, citing "irregularities" in the grand jury that resulted in his indictment.

"There is substantial evidence of grand-jury irregularities in this case," Lemon's team wrote in a recent filing.

"Multiple judges, including at the Eighth Circuit, found there was no probable cause to charge Lemon" and his co-defendant Georgia Fort, the filing said.

Mark Wolf, a former Massachusetts District Court judge and federal prosecutor, said it is rare for defense attorneys to ask for grand jury transcripts in federal court. It is even more rare that judges grant the motions, he said.

"There is a high bar to getting grand jury materials," Wolf said. "You have to have some direct or circumstantial evidence that there has been some defect in the grand jury proceeding."

In her two-page order, Provinzino wrote that she weighed the necessity of maintaining grand jury secrecy against whether grounds may exist to dismiss the case due to a "matter that occurred before the grand jury."

She did not say she had already found evidence of any misconduct.

The Justice Department's initial attempt to charge Lemon in January for appearing alongside protestors who disrupted a church service in St. Paul, Minnesota, was rejected by a federal magistrate judge, which "enraged" then Attorney General Pam Bondi, according to a source who spoke to CNN at the time.

Lemon, a former CNN anchor, was later indicted by a grand jury along with several other defendants, including independent journalist Georgia Fort. Lemon has been charged with conspiring to violate someone's constitutional rights and violating the FACE Act, which prohibits the use of force or threats to intentionally interfere with someone expressing their First Amendment right to practice religion.

Lemon has pleaded not guilty to both charges. His team has aggressively pursued obtaining grand jury materials throughout the case, and earlier this month filed a motion to dismiss the case altogether.

Wolf told CNN he does not believe the Justice Department's credibility remains intact.

"For good reasons, the Department of Justice's reputation with judges generally has been injured," Wolf said.

In Chicago, defense attorneys urged Judge April Perry to release grand jury transcripts in the highly publicized case against protestors at an ICE detention facility outside the city.

After reviewing those transcripts, Perry found federal prosecutors engaged in inappropriate actions, such as interacting with grand jurors outside the proceeding, ordering some jurors to leave in another hearing, and "vouching" to the grand jurors.

Vouching is a practice where prosecutors present their own reputation while delivering their case to a grand jury. It is forbidden in grand jury proceedings because the practice effectively asks jurors to trust the prosecutor personally rather than only on the merits of evidence.

"I have never seen the types of prosecutorial behavior before a grand jury that I saw in those transcripts," Judge Perry said during a May 21 hearing.

US Attorney Andrew Boutros then dropped the case against the protestors. Later, after reviewing the prosecutor's conduct, Boutros opted to drop at least two more criminal cases, ordered a historical review of more than 100 grand jury transcripts, and launched reforms such as more training on grand jury presentations.

"If I was a federal public defender or a private defense attorney, every case I get that's indicted, I'm going to file a motion that is asking the judge to review the transcripts," said Mike Fox, a current Cato Institute fellow and former Colorado public defender.

"In my view, at this point, it doesn't matter in which court it is, doesn't matter if I have binding case law," Fox said. "Every single case, the defense attorney should be filing, and the judge should be inquiring."

In May, a panel of three federal judges in Wyoming dismissed felony drug and gun indictments against nine defendants after the judges found the acting Wyoming US Attorney referred to defendants as "bad guys," and "murderers," and handed out business cards to jurors outside of the proceeding.

Prosecutors opted not to appeal the judges' order. Later, Wyoming federal prosecutors empaneled a new grand jury which issued a new indictment. The case remains ongoing.

Fox believes the remedy is a more engaged judiciary where judges routinely witness grand jury proceedings.

The current law doesn't require judges to listen to proceedings, but some courts are issuing new local rules to ensure greater oversight. This spring, the Northern District of Illinois, where Boutros is US Attorney, enacted a rule requiring grand juries to alert a magistrate judge when a grand jury fails to issue an indictment.

A spokesperson for the Justice Department told CNN in an email the executive office of the US Attorney provides training for prosecutors which includes grand jury practice.

"On rare occasions where there is an issue, as noted in our Chicago US Attorney's office, we took immediate corrective action and provided renewed, in-depth instruction on ethics and grand jury practice," the spokesperson wrote.

"Our US Attorneys will always follow the law and prosecute cases without fear or favor. Nobody is above the law, regardless of political affiliation. Beyond that, we don't comment on pending litigation."

Last fall, in the most high-profile and politically charged example of a problematic grand jury presentment, then-interim US Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, Lindsey Halligan, took a proposed indictment against former FBI Director James Comey through a grand jury on her own. A magistrate judge in Alexandria, Virginia, reviewed the transcript and found Halligan may have incorrectly presented the law to the grand jury. The judge called the debacle "profound investigative missteps … to potentially undermine the integrity of the grand jury proceeding."

Halligan later admitted to a judge the grand jury hadn't supported the initial version of the proposed indictment of Comey, and the full grand jury hadn't signed off on the final charging document. That Comey case was dismissed for a separate reason, when a federal district judge determined Halligan wasn't serving as a legitimate prosecutor. The Justice Department is appealing.

But the grand jury handling in the Comey case and other cases continues to hover over prosecutors.

Comey's defense team, for instance, is attempting to pry into grand jury records in the separate, newer case against him, out of Eastern North Carolina. He is charged there with threatening the president by posting on social media a photo of the numbers "8647" written in seashells on a beach.

The phrase 86 is sometimes used to say nix or get rid of something. Trump is the 47th president. Comey has denied wrongdoing in the case.

"The highly irregular procedures that led to the indictment create a significant risk that the government misrepresented key issues of fact and law to the grand jury," Comey's lawyers wrote in a recent court filing, citing federal searches of Comey that they question.

If Comey's defense cannot gain access to the grand jury transcript, they at least want a judge to look at it to check the Justice Department's work.

Wolf said he is deeply troubled by the Justice Department's recent actions and told CNN he believes it shows the American people that the department will use the law for partisan purposes.

"It sends a message that a Department of Justice that should institutionalize our ideal of equal justice under law is not doing that," Wolf said. "And that means anybody is vulnerable."

title: Mercedes' upgrades & Ferrari team orders - F1 Q&A
description: BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions after the Dutch Grand Prix.
fullText:
Lando Norris beat championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second win in a row with victoy at the Dutch Grand Prix.

Reigning world champion Norris moved up to fourth in the drivers' standings, 83 points adrift of Mercedes' Antonelli.

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen suffered heartbreak at his final home race when he crashed out heavily in the opening stages.

F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your questions after round 12 of the campaign in Zandvoort.

Is it fair to say the dominance of Mercedes is over? They haven't won a race since Spa-Francorchamps, and even then that victory wasn't consecutive. Are they focusing more now on scoring points than they are winning races?

There has been a very obvious shift in competitiveness at the front as the Formula 1 season has progressed.

Mercedes won the first six races of the season, but have won only two of the subsequent six.

Mercedes took 10 consecutive poles in the first 10 races, but have been beaten by McLaren's Lando Norris at the past two grands prix. And the fastest Mercedes was lower than second for the first time in Hungary, where Red Bull's Max Verstappen also lined up ahead of Kimi Antonelli.

Over the season as a whole so far, the Mercedes is the fastest car in qualifying by an average of 0.316 seconds over Ferrari, with McLaren a further 0.041secs adrift.

But what happens when you split that into the first six races and the next six?

Until the Canadian Grand Prix in late May, Mercedes were 0.453secs a lap faster than the next fastest team, which was McLaren at the time, and 0.489secs quicker than Ferrari.

Since Monaco, that gap has come down to 0.163secs over Ferrari and 0.270secs over McLaren. Red Bull's gap over the past six races is 0.353secs, whereas it was 0.813secs up to Canada.

There is a very obvious reason for this - Mercedes have upgraded their car less than their rivals. To a quite stark degree.

Each race, governing body the FIA issues a sheet showing the declared upgrades each team has brought to that race.

It's not a definitive list - teams don't have to put all the changes on that sheet, only the ones that are visible. But it gives an idea.

Since the start of the season, Mercedes have fitted a total of 24 new parts to their cars, compared with 37 for Red Bull, 38 for McLaren and 40 by Ferrari.

This is not a direct representation of relative spend, as some parts are more expensive than others.

But it's striking, for example, that Mercedes have also deployed fewer upgrades than Aston Martin, Alpine, Racing Bulls, Audi and Cadillac.

Even Haas, the team with the smallest budget on the grid, have had more upgrades than Mercedes, who have the equal lowest number with Williams.

This is all in the context of the budget cap, which is set at $215m (£170m) for all teams.

The question, obviously, is what is going on here?

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says: "We haven't got the money to put developments on the car.

"We are trying to evenly split that through the season, based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points. But we just can do what we can do."

Asked why McLaren and Ferrari appeared to have the money and Mercedes did not, Wolff said: "Well, you will see how towards the end of the season (whether) they are going to be able to deploy as much stuff on to the car as they do now.

"Someone might have a different strategy in spending more at the beginning and in the middle of the year than towards the end."

The obvious conclusion is that Mercedes either spent more money in the design and build process of this year's car than their rivals - which would make sense, given how competitive it was at the start of the season - or they have saved money to spend on their next upgrade, and/or next year's car.

That is due at the so-called Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October, when there are either eight or nine grands prix remaining, depending on the situation in the Middle East.

On top of that, Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the next race in Italy for exceeding the permitted number of engine parts, and George Russell will also have one at a subsequent race, most likely Azerbaijan.

Mercedes lack money to develop car like rivals - Wolff

Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' who started driving on dad's lap

How did the alleged improvements go on the Aston Martin? Is there any sign of improved performance? - Chris

Honda gave a debut to its long-awaited 'spec two' engine at the Dutch Grand Prix, while Aston Martin added a new front wing and diffuser to the pretty much all-new car that was introduced at the previous race in Hungary.

Within the team, they were hoping that the Honda engine would reduce lap times by somewhere in the region of 0.3-0.5secs.

The weekend painted a confusing picture.

On the one hand, Fernando Alonso looked more competitive than ever before at various points.

But he qualified further away from pole in both positional and percentage terms than he had in Hungary.

There were, however, extenuating circumstances, in that he was 12th fastest before failing to improve on a messy final lap hindered by a sub-optimal 'prep' lap which left his tyres out of the 'window'. Without that, he probably would have progressed beyond the first session.

Nevertheless, that suggests the new Honda was little better than the old one. On the other hand, the new engine's drivability was definitely worse, which may have skewed the picture.

But then Alonso drove an outstanding race on a one-stop strategy to take ninth place, looking after tyres and measuring his pace with all the expertise and skill he has shown throughout his career to hold off two faster cars in Pierre Gasly's Alpine and Yuki Tsunoda's Racing Bull in the final stint.

Those are the first points Aston Martin have scored on merit all season.

As Alonso put it: "We scored one point in Monaco with nine DNFs (retirements). Today we scored two points with Max (Verstappen) DNF. It was well deserved."

Alonso said after the race that the team were planning a two-stop but changed during the race because they were stuck behind other cars.

"We are in traffic," he said. "We cannot use our potential. We are faster in the corners than the people in front of us and we are slower on the straights. We're stuck behind.

"So as soon as we have free track in front of us, we try to use it. Even if it's not the optimal performance and the optimal strategy, and it's what we did today."

On the car and engine upgrades, Alonso said: "Another step forward, especially on the chassis side.

"We brought four or five components here. Also the Budapest package was understood in the (summer) break. With all the data available after the race, we fine-tuned a little bit the set-up around that new spec. Plus the new parts. I think now we are optimising the chassis side and we are able to extract the maximum.

"The engine is more difficult. I don't think we can be black and white if we have more power or not.

"On the driver side of things, you change circuits one month after the other race. The drivability has been a difficult weekend. We struggled with the downshift again. We struggled with the engine braking corner to corner. It was a challenging weekend in that regard."

These engines are highly complex and it takes time for teams to dial into them so they are working at their optimum. So it may be a few more races before the new Honda can be judged fairly.

Did Charles Leclerc cost Ferrari and Lewis Hamilton a podium position by holding Hamilton up when he refused to pit when instructed to, and what will Ferrari do to ensure he follows team orders in the future? - Mike

Mid-race in Zandvoort, Lewis Hamilton came up behind Charles Leclerc on fresher tyres, their strategies offset, and asked to be let by to optimise his race.

The way the television broadcast was played out, it sounded as if Ferrari decided to pit Leclerc for fresh tyres to get him out of the way. He initially resisted that and did not come in, but then came in at the next call.

Team boss Frederic Vasseur addressed this after the race, in comments that were a little unclear.

First, he said, at that point, Ferrari were thinking of running Hamilton to the end, so they did not want him to push hard - but had not told him that was the case, because they wanted to keep the plan secret from their rivals.

As for Leclerc, Vasseur said they were "expecting him to pit" but then realised he was in danger of coming out in traffic.

Vasseur said: "Charles was supposed to pit, we extended one lap, and it was a kind of confusion, but I'm not worried about this. Everybody will be back in the briefing, they will have a clear picture about the race."

Some will inevitably say this was another example of Ferrari messing up their strategy, an accusation that is levelled at them quite often.

Vasseur said: "It's not so easy, but, if I look at the race now, my issue is that we didn't tell Lewis that we were expecting him to go to the end, and it was not a matter of (him) pushing (at that point)."

Did the delay cost Hamilton third? Hamilton thought so, but it's impossible to know whether he would have passed George Russell if he had had a lap or two more to try.

With Isack Hadjar hurting his wrist during the summer break, do teams not ask drivers to stay away from high impact or dangerous sports and activity during their time off to keep them ready for their return? - Dave

F1 drivers' contracts usually have clauses in them forbidding them from doing 'dangerous sports', such as skiing or scuba diving, although not every driver's contract is the same.

In Hadjar's case, the Frenchman suffered what Red Bull describe as a "minor fracture" while doing a boxing exercise which is part of his normal gym routine.

There is no suggestion of him doing anything that could have been outside the terms of his contract.

Red Bull are targeting for him to return for the next race, the Italian Grand Prix, but it remains to be seen whether that will be possible.

title: £1.5m-rated Abdulmalik asks to leave Boreham Wood
description: Boreham Wood forward Abdul Abdulmalik says he is "capable of reaching the top" after the National League side reject a £1.5m offer from Swedish club Djurgarden.
fullText:
Boreham Wood forward Abdul Abdulmalik said he is "capable of reaching the top" after the National League side rejected a £1.5m offer from Swedish club Djurgarden.

The 23-year-old has been the subject of serious interest from the Swedish top-flight side, who had an offer of £1m rejected earlier this month.

Boreham Wood do not want to sell Abdulmalik, with manager Luke Garrard saying "he is our player" after the forward was left out of the London club's 3-0 victory over Forest Green on Saturday.

"Everyone at Boreham Wood FC and the incredible fans have played a massive part [in my journey]. You will always have my respect," Adbulmalik said in a statement released by his agent.

"With this said, I'm ready for the next challenge. I'm ready to prove to myself and those around me that I'm capable of reaching the top."

Abdulmalik enjoyed a breakout season in 2025-26, scoring 17 goals and providing 10 assists as Boreham Wood reached the National League play-off final, where he scored and assisted at Wembley.

Djurgarden's £1.5m offer would have broken the record fee paid for a fifth-tier player in England, set in 2012 when Leicester paid Fleetwood Town £1m for Jamie Vardy.

"Through sheer hard work and perseverance, the opportunity to progress has come around. This is my chance to push myself as a footballer, elevate my game and most importantly fulfil my promise to the ones around me," Abdulmalik continued.

"Opportunities like this are rare, especially within the National League where some of the hardest working talent is overlooked.

"The game of football is forever changing and decisions are fast paced. There's no guarantee that the same chances come knocking twice.

"I owe it to myself and the kids growing up just like me to fight for this one I've been offered."

Abdulmalik came through Millwall's academy, progressing through the club's youth system and representing England at under-17 level.

He was part of the club's Under-21s successes - securing consecutive Professional Development League South titles in 2022-23 and 2023-24.

However, a pathway into consistent first-team football did not materialise and Abdulmalik was released in 2024, before Boreham Wood signed him as a free agent.

BBC Sport has contacted Boreham Wood for comment.

title: Cole leaves role as England U21 coach
description: Ashley Cole leaves his role as England Under-21 coach after five years in the position.
fullText:
Ashley Cole has left his role as an England Under-21 coach after five years in the position.

The former Chelsea and Arsenal defender was part of Lee Carsley's coaching team which guided the side to back-to-back European Under-21 titles.

Carsley said the 45-year-old Cole, who retired from playing in 2019 before going into coaching, had a "positive, inspirational impact on his players".

"I want to pay tribute to Ashley who played a major part in our two Euro wins and also had a key role in the current campaign with his tactical and technical knowledge," he added.

"I am certain he will have even more success in his coaching career whatever the future holds."

After completing his coaching badges at Derby County under Frank Lampard, Cole worked in Chelsea's academy before further spells assisting managers at Everton, Birmingham City - under Wayne Rooney - and then England during Carsley's brief spell as interim boss of the senior side in 2024.

Cole took over as head coach of Serie B club Cesena in March after feeling "discouraged" within the English football pyramid from succeeding in a managerial role.

He left the role in June, external after discussions with the club's sporting director regarding a "change in the club's strategy".

As a player Cole won 107 England caps and secured multiple trophies with Arsenal and Chelsea, including three Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Europa League, seven FA Cups and one League Cup.

title: All the best Savinho - welcome Savio... new club, new name for Spurs signing
description: Tottenham sign Brazil winger Savinho from Manchester City for an initial £75m - and he reverts to being called Savio.
fullText:
"Wishing you all the best, Savinho", wrote Manchester City on social media platform X, external.

"Welcome to Tottenham, Savio", announced Spurs., external

The 22-year-old Brazil winger has joined the Londoners for an initial fee of £75m - and a new start has come with a new name.

Or, should we say, his actual name.

In 2024 he said his national team put Savinho on his shirt, and he asked City to keep it for luck when he moved there in 2024.

But now the attacker, whose full name is Savio Moreira de Oliveira, has reverted back and will be known as Savio on his number 17 shirt, not Savinho.

He has signed a long-term contract, with Roberto de Zerbi's side potentially paying a further £10m in add-ons.

Savio's move to north London has been more than 12 months in the making, with Spurs failing in a bid to sign him last summer when Thomas Frank was in charge.

He opted to remain at Etihad Stadium, but his game time was limited under former City boss Pep Guardiola last term, making just seven Premier League starts.

"It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here," said Savio, who has 13 caps for his country but was not part of their World Cup squad.

"It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

"As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team."

Savio joined City from French side Troyes in a £30.8m deal two years ago and made 84 appearances, scoring seven goals and providing 16 assists.

His arrival at Spurs follows those of Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton this summer, with spending reaching a combined £312m.

Spurs have also brought in defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, and goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, on free transfers.

"Savio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity," added De Zerbi.

Spurs are also in advanced talks to buy Egypt forward Omar Marmoush from City, and sources with knowledge of the situation say there is a "good chance" the deal gets completed before the 1 September transfer deadline.

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window?

Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

Savio's involvement for City fell sharply last season after the club signed winger Antoine Semenyo from Bournemouth in January.

He played 821 Premier League minutes, scoring once and providing one assist, while featuring in only 31% of City's available minutes across all competitions.

That was a significant drop from the previous campaign, when he played 54% of City's minutes.

Yet his 2024-25 numbers show why Tottenham are prepared to invest heavily in him. Savio registered eight Premier League assists that season, all from open play, despite playing only 1,773 minutes. Only five players recorded more from open play.

On a per-90 basis, he ranked third for open-play assists with 0.41, while only Mohamed Salah created more chances per 90 than Savio's 2.2.

His biggest threat, though, came from carrying the ball. Among Premier League players with at least 1,000 minutes in 2024-25, only Jeremy Doku averaged more progressive carries of at least 10 metres than Savio's 6.8 per 90 minutes.

Savio also led the division for carries followed by a chance created, averaging 1.3 per 90, while only Son Heung-min ended a carry with an assist more frequently. Savio also completed 2.6 dribbles per 90 with a 51% success rate and used those carries to draw defenders towards him before releasing team-mates.

That ability was even more evident during his breakout 2023-24 season on loan at Girona. Savio played 2,989 minutes in La Liga in 2023-24, with 65% of them coming on the left wing. He scored nine goals, supplied eight assists and established himself as one of the division's most dangerous one-against-one players.

At City his role shifted. Across his two Premier League seasons, his most common position was on the right, accounting for 36% of his minutes, compared with 20% on the left. That versatility could matter at Spurs.
